external_evidence.title: package.json pins js-yaml@4.3.1 / yaml<2.9 to known CVE ranges (GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh, GHSA-48c2-rrv3-qjmp)
external_evidence.body:
### Summary
`package.json` pins `js-yaml` to exactly the vulnerable range of [GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh) (CPU DoS via empty merge sources; fixed in 4.3.2), and the transitive `yaml` dependency sits below the fix for [GHSA-48c2-rrv3-qjmp](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-48c2-rrv3-qjmp) (stack overflow via deeply nested collections; fixed in 2.9.1). `npm audit` therefore reports 2 high + 1 moderate on a clean install.

### Details
- `overrides` pins `"js-yaml@^4": "4.3.1"` and `dependencies` pins `"js-yaml": "4.3.1"` — 4.3.1 is the last vulnerable release (advisory covers 4.0.0–4.3.1).
- `yaml` ≤2.8.2 arrives transitively (e.g. via `electron-updater` → `js-yaml`, and `apps/desktop` declares `"yaml": "2.8.1"`).
- `npm audit fix --force` cannot resolve it: `EOVERRIDE: Override for js-yaml@4.3.2 conflicts with direct dependency`.
- Additionally `.npmrc` sets `min-release-age=14`, which hides the patched releases (`yaml@2.9.1`, `js-yaml@4.3.2`) until they age in. `js-yaml` already has a `min-release-age-exclude[]` entry, but `yaml` does not.

### Suggested fix
Bump `overrides`/`dependencies`/lockfile to `js-yaml@4.3.2+` and `yaml@2.9.1+`, and add `min-release-age-exclude[]=yaml` (or widen the existing exclusions) so the patched versions are installable.

*(Filed from a local audit of v0.21.5+2085.gda931c9; locally mitigated by patching the pins, but the fix reverts on every `hermes update` since it reinstalls from the committed lockfile.)*

Covered by #122537 (opened first, same files, same direction): it bumps root js-yaml 4.3.1 -> 4.3.2 and apps/desktop yaml 2.8.1 -> 2.9.0, but does not reference this issue. Equivalence evidence from the advisory DB:

- GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh (js-yaml): vulnerable >= 4.0.0, < 4.3.2, first patched 4.3.2. Their 4.3.2 clears it.
- GHSA-48c2-rrv3-qjmp (yaml): vulnerable >= 2.0.0, < 2.8.3, first patched 2.8.3. Their 2.9.0 (rel 2026-05-11, past the 14-day min-release-age gate, so no .npmrc exclude needed) clears it. Note the issue body says fixed in 2.9.1, but the DB first-patched is 2.8.3, so 2.9.0 is sufficient.

One remaining gap after #122537: website/package.json still overrides js-yaml to 4.3.1 and website/package-lock.json still locks node_modules/js-yaml 4.3.1 (website is a separate install scope, so root npm audit stays clean, but a website install still pulls the vulnerable version). Suggest a follow-up bump there once #122537 lands to avoid lockfile conflicts. Not pushing a duplicate PR for the root/desktop pins.

**Independent reproduction from a local audit — not a competing proposal.** I hit the same pins on a local install today, applied the bump locally, and measured the result. Posting the parts that look new relative to the issue body and to #106158 / #122199 / #122537.

**Environment.** Hermes Agent v0.21.5 (upstream `fdec926e`, install method: git), Node 26.10.0, npm 11.19.1, clean tree at HEAD.

### 1. The bump reifies through the pipeline's own install step

Changed only the two root pins — `dependencies.js-yaml` and `overrides["js-yaml@^4"]`, both `4.3.1` → `4.3.2` — and regenerated the lockfile with `npm install --package-lock-only`: 4 lines changed in `package-lock.json` (version, `resolved`, `integrity`, plus the root dependency record), no other package re-resolved.

Then reified with the update's own dependency step rather than a manual `npm ci`:

```
node scripts/build/node-deps.mjs --source <root> --reuse --workspace ui-tui --workspace web
```

and the next invocation logged `node-deps: reusing completed install (ui-tui, web)`, i.e. the `node_modules/.hermes-node-deps` receipt matches the new lockfile — so an `hermes update` on the same tree will not fight the bump.

Result: installed `js-yaml` is 4.3.2; `npm audit` reports **0** vulnerabilities in the root scope (the one `hermes doctor` audits with `--workspaces=false`), and 3 moderate each in `ui-tui` and `web` (`vitest`, `@vitest/mocker`, `yaml`). No scope lists `js-yaml` any more. (That install path provisions only the `ui-tui` and `web` workspaces, so the `apps/desktop` tree is not present in that `node_modules`; the desktop-scoped findings from the issue body do not appear there.)

### 2. The `min-release-age` gate is not what holds this bump

Both `/.npmrc` and `/website/.npmrc` already carry `min-release-age-exclude[]=js-yaml` (added for GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj, commented "remove when > 2wks old (rel 2026-07-31)"), with `min-release-age=14` in both. 4.3.2 was released 2026-08-26, so it is also ~30 days old. A manifest+lockfile bump therefore has no age gate to clear — the `js-yaml` pin is simply stale, not age-blocked. (`yaml` is the other half of this issue and has no exclude entry, as the issue body already notes.)

### 3. Post-fix behaviour, measured

With 4.3.2 installed, the advisory's payload (N empty mappings aliased, then merged K times) is refused in ~8 ms with `abnormal merge sequence size`. Before the bump the same shape parsed and consumed CPU quadratically — 13.5 / 30.7 / 102.4 ms for N = 1000 / 2000 / 4000 (same order as the advisory's own PoC table). A normal merge document (`<<: *anchor` over a small mapping) still parses identically, so the new hard limit (merge sequence > 100) is the only behaviour change, and nothing in this install hits it. I also rebuilt both frontends through the update's own path (`python -m hermes_cli.source_build --source .`): TUI and web UI build cleanly.

### 4. One concrete note for whoever picks up the bot PR

#106158 (dependabot) touches `package-lock.json` **only**. With the root manifest keeping the exact pins — `4.3.1` in both `dependencies` and the `overrides` entry — a lockfile-only move cannot be reified by the pipeline's `npm ci`. Reproduced in a minimal project with the same shape (exact direct pin + exact override):

```
npm error code EUSAGE
npm error `npm ci` can only install packages when your package.json and
npm error package-lock.json or npm-shrinkwrap.json are in sync.
npm error Invalid: lock file's js-yaml@4.3.2 does not satisfy js-yaml@4.3.1
```

So that PR needs the manifest change to land together with the lockfile change. #122199 and #122537 do change the manifest.

### 5. Confirming the remaining gap flagged in the earlier comment

On this checkout `website/package.json` still overrides `js-yaml` to `4.3.1`, and `website/package-lock.json` still locks `node_modules/js-yaml` at 4.3.1 — a separate install scope, so the root audit stays clean while a website install still pulls the vulnerable version.

---

For completeness: my change is a deliberate local divergence with no commit on this checkout; the fix reverts on every `hermes update` (as the issue body and #116774 describe), and the detector is `hermes doctor` re-reporting it. No claim on authorship of the fix — just reproduction and measurements, in case they help one of the open PRs land.

# Comment for nousresearch/hermes-agent#122424
# Post with: gh issue comment 122424 --repo nousresearch/hermes-agent --body-file /tmp/comment-122424.md

Third independent verification of the fix direction, plus a **pipeline-shape test of #122537 that the thread hasn't covered yet** — whether the PR's *combined* manifest+lockfile change survives the update's own deterministic install.

**Environment.** Hermes Agent v0.21.5 (upstream `f8123d2401`, git install, clean worktree at origin/main — the pins cited below were grepped from that tree, not a patched one), Node 26.7.0, npm 12.0.2.

### 1. The PR's exact diff applies clean and `npm ci` accepts it — twice

Applied the full diff of #122537 to a throwaway worktree at `f8123d2401` (files: root + apps/desktop + tests-js + ui-tui + web package.jsons and package-lock.json; `git apply --check` clean). Then reified with the update pipeline's own install step:

- `npm ci` (npm 12.0.2): **completes** — no `EUSAGE` / `Invalid: lock file's js-yaml@4.3.2 does not satisfy js-yaml@4.3.1` failure that a lockfile-only bump produces (as @ClaudioDrews reproduced for #106158's shape in this thread). Manifest and lockfile in #122537 are mutually consistent.
- A second consecutive `npm ci` also completes — the lockfile is idempotent under the deterministic reinstall, so an `hermes update` won't fight or revert it.
- Root scope (`npm audit --workspaces=false`, the scope `hermes doctor` audits): **0 vulnerabilities**. Root js-yaml resolves to 4.3.2.

### 2. Post-PR residuals are exactly the pre-tracked set

`npm audit` on the full PR tree reports 4 remaining, none new, all already covered in #107356:

- `@xmldom/xmldom` high — root copy still at 0.8.13 (tests-js copy is 0.9.12 via the PR); fix within range, no --force needed
- `electron` + `extract-zip` high — desktop tree at 40.10.2 (the #107356 / #92921 subject; fixed in 40.10.6 per the advisory)
- `joi` low — 18.2.3; fix within range

So landing #122537 plus the #107356 residuals takes the full tree to 0; I measured exactly that combined state locally (root js-yaml 4.3.2 + override, yaml 2.9.1, vitest 4.1.11 in all four workspaces, @xmldom/xmldom 0.8.15/0.9.12, joi 18.2.9) → full-tree audit 0, `hermes doctor` "All checks passed".

### 3. Age-gate math for the residual bumps (for whoever picks up #107356)

`min-release-age=14` in `.npmrc`; measured publish dates from the registry: js-yaml 4.3.2 (2026-08-26), vitest 4.1.11 (2026-08-18), @xmldom/xmldom 0.9.12/0.8.15 (2026-08-21) — all past the gate today. yaml 2.9.1 (2026-09-11) is right AT the 14-day boundary as of filing, and `.npmrc` has no `min-release-age-exclude[]=yaml` entry (only js-yaml is excluded), so the exclude entry the issue body suggests may still be needed for that one bump.

### 4. A note on the vitest alias entries

The PR's `"vitest": "vitest.mjs"` devDependency aliases (tests-js, ui-tui) are the #119059 workaround; they resolve correctly in the PR tree (`npm ls vitest` → 4.1.11) and the alias form doesn't disturb `npm ci`. Worth keeping in mind that apps/shared still imports vitest without declaring it (#119059), so the alias entries shouldn't be dropped as "redundant" in review.

---

Verification was done in a disposable worktree at `f8123d2401`, since removed; my own install keeps the same bumps locally. No claim on the fix — just pipeline evidence that #122537's shape is the right one to merge.

Fixed upstream: as of cda237464a the checkout's package.json pins `js-yaml@^4: 4.3.2` and `yaml@^2: 2.9.1` (verified directly in the updated tree), and `npm audit` reports 0 vulnerabilities without any local overlay. Closing. (Local .npmrc min-release-age notes in this issue may still be relevant for future bumps — see #122424 body.)

### Re-verified on current `main`: the pins are still vulnerable — this closure's cited commit contains no bump

Not reopening for the sake of it — the verification quoted in the closing comment does not hold, and the vulnerable pins are live on `main` as of today.

**Environment.** Git install, fresh clone at `d25bbd01b75cf2d472a88857af7b7f056dd0f9f7` (`git ls-remote origin main` agrees; `hermes --version` reports "Up to date"). Version string `v0.21.5+3397.gd25bbd0`.

**1. The cited fix commit contains no dependency change.**

```
$ git log -1 --format='%h%n%cI%n%s' cda237464a
cda237464a51739e55ab13946a00272e548443e5
2026-09-26T07:14:26+05:30
test(bedrock): record a missing metadata match as a mismatch, not a TypeError
```

`cda237464a` is a bedrock test commit. The manifest at that commit is unchanged from the vulnerable state:

```
$ git show cda237464a:package.json | grep -n 'js-yaml'
58:    "js-yaml@^4": "4.3.1",
79:    "js-yaml": "4.3.1",
```

**2. Nothing has bumped it between that commit and HEAD.**

```
$ git show HEAD:package.json | grep -n 'js-yaml'
58:    "js-yaml@^4": "4.3.1",
79:    "js-yaml": "4.3.1"

$ git log --format='%h %cI %s' cda237464a..HEAD -- package.json
(no output)
```

**3. A clean tree still audits dirty, and doctor still flags it.**

```
$ npm audit --workspaces=false
# metadata.vulnerabilities: { high: 1, total: 1 }
# js-yaml >=4.0.0 <4.3.2 — GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh (CVSS 7.5)
```

`hermes doctor` on the same tree: `⚠ Browser tools (agent-browser) deps (0 critical, 1 high, 0 moderate — fix is an upstream lockfile bump — a local manual fix does not persist ... #116774)`. (That row audits the repo ROOT tree with `--workspaces=false`, per `hermes_cli/doctor_tools.py::_check_npm_audit` — the label does not name the directory it audits.)

**4. The second advisory in the original report is also still open here.** `apps/desktop/package.json` at HEAD still pins `"yaml": "2.8.1"`, below the first-patched `2.8.3` for GHSA-48c2-rrv3-qjmp.

### The real blocker looks like the dupe pile, not the fix

Ten open PRs currently carry this same bump: #106158, #110444, #122199, #122537, #122775, #122884, #123082, #123537, #123671, #124233. I am deliberately not adding an eleventh. Any one of them landing resolves it; the observable problem today is that `main` is still on 4.3.1 while this issue reads as resolved, so nobody re-checks.

### Local mitigation (for anyone hitting it meanwhile)

Both root pins bumped to `4.3.2` + `npm install --workspaces=false` clears the root audit to `found 0 vulnerabilities`, and the module loads/parses normally afterwards. As the doctor text says, this is not durable — `hermes update` reinstalls from the committed lockfile — which is exactly why it needs to land upstream.

# REOPEN!

This was never fixed, and mixing *carreted* (`^`) package definitions always fails!
作者重开：此前关闭依据（cda237464a）实为无依赖变更的测试提交，@jauhubbot 复核成立——重开补正审计轨迹后按实装证据再裁决。

# 更正审计与结案（作者重开后复核，2026-09-28，v0.21.5+3962 @ 37daf85b2a）

先认账：**本单此前的关闭依据是错的**。@jauhubbot 的复核完全成立——我引用的 `cda237464a` 是 bedrock 测试提交，不含任何依赖变更，且该提交处 `js-yaml` 仍是 4.3.1。关闭时（09-26）漏洞钉版确实还在 `main` 上。@eabase 的 REOPEN 诉求因此在时间线上是对的。感谢两位把关。

## 但修复本身随后真的落地了——落在 d25bbd01b7..37daf85b2a（565 提交波）内

| 证据点 | js-yaml | yaml | 来源 |
|---|---|---|---|
| d25bbd01b7（09-27，@jauhubbot git show） | 4.3.1 | <2.9 形态 | 本单评论 |
| 37daf85b2a（09-28，我 grep package.json） | **4.3.2**（L58 `js-yaml@^4`→4.3.2、L80→4.3.2） | **2.9.1**（L59 `yaml@^2`→2.9.1） | 直读 HEAD manifest |
| 实际解析树（今晨 npm ls） | **js-yaml@4.3.2 overridden** | **yaml@2.9.1**（vite 链 deduped） | node_modules 实装 |

即 bump 发生在两核验点之间的那一波更新里（精确提交归属暂缺：本机 git 仓库处于 auto-packing 退化态，`git log -S`/范围 log 均超时，不硬猜提交号——如需要，上游可在两 tag 间 `git log -- package.json` 一击定位）。

## 对 @eabase「carreted (^) 必败」的商榷

overrides 里 `"js-yaml@^4": "4.3.2"` 的写法是 npm 标准语义：**键是范围选择器、值是精确钉版**——`npm ls` 实测显示 `js-yaml@4.3.2 overridden`，即任何传递依赖请求 js-yaml@^4 都被强制解析到 4.3.2，树里无 4.3.1 残留（`npm ls` 未列出任何 4.3.1 节点）。混用 caret 键本身不构成漏洞通道；关键是值是精确版且实装生效。

## 结论

漏洞钉版 4.3.1 / yaml<2.9 **已在 565 提交波内实际拔除**，实装树干净。本单重开是为了给错误的关闭依据补正审计轨迹，补正完成，**依实装证据再次关闭**。若后续在任何分支/波次再见 4.3.1 回潮，凭 `npm ls js-yaml yaml` 一图即可重开。
依实装证据关闭：4.3.1/yaml<2.9 已于 d25bbd01b7..37daf85b2a 波内拔除（HEAD manifest L58/L59/L80 + npm ls 实装树 js-yaml@4.3.2 overridden / yaml@2.9.1 双证）。详见更正审计评论。
第三次重开并保持 OPEN：干净室取证确认上游 main 至今仍钉 js-yaml 4.3.1（此前两次关闭均误——第二次把本机 autostash 本地补丁当上游状态）。eabase 所要的完整 diff 已附。

# 第三次重开——这次我方两个错误一起认，证据链闭合（2026-09-28，v0.21.5+4151 @ 8f21606116）

@jauhubbot @eabase 两位全程正确，我方连错两次，向你们致歉。这次把干净室取证做全：

## 错误复盘（两次关闭各错一处）

1. **第一次关闭（09-26）**：引用 cda237464a 为修复提交——实为 bedrock 测试提交零依赖变更（@jauhubbot 当场证伪）；
2. **第二次关闭（今晨）**：我 grep 的是**工作树** package.json（4.3.2/2.9.1），却归因给 37daf85b2a 提交——工作树里躺着一份**本机本地补丁**（每次 update 靠 autostash 往返存活），我把它误当成了上游状态。@eabase「I don't see any of those upgraded in your posted PR's」完全正确：**从来没有 PR，也从来没有上游提交**。

## 干净室证据（v0.21.5+4151 @ 8f21606116，逐字）

上游提交内容（`git show HEAD:package.json`）：

    58:    "js-yaml@^4": "4.3.1",
    79:    "js-yaml": "4.3.1",

——**上游 main 至今仍钉 4.3.1，且无 yaml@^2 覆盖**。CVE（GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh / GHSA-48c2-rrv3-qjmp）影响面维持。

本机工作树（=本地补丁，`git diff HEAD -- package.json` 完整 diff，即 eabase 所要）：

    @@ -55,7 +55,8 @@
    -    "js-yaml@^4": "4.3.1",
    +    "js-yaml@^4": "4.3.2",
    +    "yaml@^2": "2.9.1",
    @@ -76,7 +77,7 @@
    -    "js-yaml": "4.3.1",
    +    "js-yaml": "4.3.2",

配套 `npm ls js-yaml yaml` 实装树（在补丁作用下）：js-yaml@4.3.2 overridden / yaml@2.9.1——证明这 4 行补丁语义有效、可直接上游化。

## 处置

本单**保持 OPEN**——这是真实的上游漏洞单，不再由我关闭。修复现成：上面 4 行 diff 可直接应用（overrides 键 `js-yaml@^4`/`yaml@^2` 是 npm 标准范围选择器+精确值，@eabase 的 carret 担忧在「值为精确版」前提下不成立，实装树已证）。若维护者要我以 PR 形式提交，说一声即开分支上。

另：本机为防 CVE 长期带着该补丁（update autostash 往返）——这也解释了我此前所有「已修复」误判的来源，取证规范教训已内化：**验证上游状态必须 `git show HEAD:`，工作树在 autostash 机上不是证据**。

Time to migrate!
https://github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/blob/master/docs/migrate_v4_to_v5.md
赞同 v5 迁移是终局（v5 是 semver major，独立成单更干净）。当下最小修复=4.3.2 钉版 bump（本单已附 4 行 diff，无破坏性）；v5 迁移可作为后续跟进项，两者不冲突。

external_evidence.description:
### Summary
`package.json` pins `js-yaml` to exactly the vulnerable range of [GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh) (CPU DoS via empty merge sources; fixed in 4.3.2), and the transitive `yaml` dependency sits below the fix for [GHSA-48c2-rrv3-qjmp](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-48c2-rrv3-qjmp) (stack overflow via deeply nested collections; fixed in 2.9.1). `npm audit` therefore reports 2 high + 1 moderate on a clean install.

### Details
- `overrides` pins `"js-yaml@^4": "4.3.1"` and `dependencies` pins `"js-yaml": "4.3.1"` — 4.3.1 is the last vulnerable release (advisory covers 4.0.0–4.3.1).
- `yaml` ≤2.8.2 arrives transitively (e.g. via `electron-updater` → `js-yaml`, and `apps/desktop` declares `"yaml": "2.8.1"`).
- `npm audit fix --force` cannot resolve it: `EOVERRIDE: Override for js-yaml@4.3.2 conflicts with direct dependency`.
- Additionally `.npmrc` sets `min-release-age=14`, which hides the patched releases (`yaml@2.9.1`, `js-yaml@4.3.2`) until they age in. `js-yaml` already has a `min-release-age-exclude[]` entry, but `yaml` does not.

### Suggested fix
Bump `overrides`/`dependencies`/lockfile to `js-yaml@4.3.2+` and `yaml@2.9.1+`, and add `min-release-age-exclude[]=yaml` (or widen the existing exclusions) so the patched versions are installable.

*(Filed from a local audit of v0.21.5+2085.gda931c9; locally mitigated by patching the pins, but the fix reverts on every `hermes update` since it reinstalls from the committed lockfile.)*


--- Issue comments ---
Covered by #122537 (opened first, same files, same direction): it bumps root js-yaml 4.3.1 -> 4.3.2 and apps/desktop yaml 2.8.1 -> 2.9.0, but does not reference this issue. Equivalence evidence from the advisory DB:

- GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh (js-yaml): vulnerable >= 4.0.0, < 4.3.2, first patched 4.3.2. Their 4.3.2 clears it.
- GHSA-48c2-rrv3-qjmp (yaml): vulnerable >= 2.0.0, < 2.8.3, first patched 2.8.3. Their 2.9.0 (rel 2026-05-11, past the 14-day min-release-age gate, so no .npmrc exclude needed) clears it. Note the issue body says fixed in 2.9.1, but the DB first-patched is 2.8.3, so 2.9.0 is sufficient.

One remaining gap after #122537: website/package.json still overrides js-yaml to 4.3.1 and website/package-lock.json still locks node_modules/js-yaml 4.3.1 (website is a separate install scope, so root npm audit stays clean, but a website install still pulls the vulnerable version). Suggest a follow-up bump there once #122537 lands to avoid lockfile conflicts. Not pushing a duplicate PR for the root/desktop pins.

**Independent reproduction from a local audit — not a competing proposal.** I hit the same pins on a local install today, applied the bump locally, and measured the result. Posting the parts that look new relative to the issue body and to #106158 / #122199 / #122537.

**Environment.** Hermes Agent v0.21.5 (upstream `fdec926e`, install method: git), Node 26.10.0, npm 11.19.1, clean tree at HEAD.

### 1. The bump reifies through the pipeline's own install step

Changed only the two root pins — `dependencies.js-yaml` and `overrides["js-yaml@^4"]`, both `4.3.1` → `4.3.2` — and regenerated the lockfile with `npm install --package-lock-only`: 4 lines changed in `package-lock.json` (version, `resolved`, `integrity`, plus the root dependency record), no other package re-resolved.

Then reified with the update's own dependency step rather than a manual `npm ci`:

```
node scripts/build/node-deps.mjs --source <root> --reuse --workspace ui-tui --workspace web
```

and the next invocation logged `node-deps: reusing completed install (ui-tui, web)`, i.e. the `node_modules/.hermes-node-deps` receipt matches the new lockfile — so an `hermes update` on the same tree will not fight the bump.

Result: installed `js-yaml` is 4.3.2; `npm audit` reports **0** vulnerabilities in the root scope (the one `hermes doctor` audits with `--workspaces=false`), and 3 moderate each in `ui-tui` and `web` (`vitest`, `@vitest/mocker`, `yaml`). No scope lists `js-yaml` any more. (That install path provisions only the `ui-tui` and `web` workspaces, so the `apps/desktop` tree is not present in that `node_modules`; the desktop-scoped findings from the issue body do not appear there.)

### 2. The `min-release-age` gate is not what holds this bump

Both `/.npmrc` and `/website/.npmrc` already carry `min-release-age-exclude[]=js-yaml` (added for GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj, commented "remove when > 2wks old (rel 2026-07-31)"), with `min-release-age=14` in both. 4.3.2 was released 2026-08-26, so it is also ~30 days old. A manifest+lockfile bump therefore has no age gate to clear — the `js-yaml` pin is simply stale, not age-blocked. (`yaml` is the other half of this issue and has no exclude entry, as the issue body already notes.)

### 3. Post-fix behaviour, measured

With 4.3.2 installed, the advisory's payload (N empty mappings aliased, then merged K times) is refused in ~8 ms with `abnormal merge sequence size`. Before the bump the same shape parsed and consumed CPU quadratically — 13.5 / 30.7 / 102.4 ms for N = 1000 / 2000 / 4000 (same order as the advisory's own PoC table). A normal merge document (`<<: *anchor` over a small mapping) still parses identically, so the new hard limit (merge sequence > 100) is the only behaviour change, and nothing in this install hits it. I also rebuilt both frontends through the update's own path (`python -m hermes_cli.source_build --source .`): TUI and web UI build cleanly.

### 4. One concrete note for whoever picks up the bot PR

#106158 (dependabot) touches `package-lock.json` **only**. With the root manifest keeping the exact pins — `4.3.1` in both `dependencies` and the `overrides` entry — a lockfile-only move cannot be reified by the pipeline's `npm ci`. Reproduced in a minimal project with the same shape (exact direct pin + exact override):

```
npm error code EUSAGE
npm error `npm ci` can only install packages when your package.json and
npm error package-lock.json or npm-shrinkwrap.json are in sync.
npm error Invalid: lock file's js-yaml@4.3.2 does not satisfy js-yaml@4.3.1
```

So that PR needs the manifest change to land together with the lockfile change. #122199 and #122537 do change the manifest.

### 5. Confirming the remaining gap flagged in the earlier comment

On this checkout `website/package.json` still overrides `js-yaml` to `4.3.1`, and `website/package-lock.json` still locks `node_modules/js-yaml` at 4.3.1 — a separate install scope, so the root audit stays clean while a website install still pulls the vulnerable version.

---

For completeness: my change is a deliberate local divergence with no commit on this checkout; the fix reverts on every `hermes update` (as the issue body and #116774 describe), and the detector is `hermes doctor` re-reporting it. No claim on authorship of the fix — just reproduction and measurements, in case they help one of the open PRs land.


# Comment for nousresearch/hermes-agent#122424
# Post with: gh issue comment 122424 --repo nousresearch/hermes-agent --body-file /tmp/comment-122424.md

Third independent verification of the fix direction, plus a **pipeline-shape test of #122537 that the thread hasn't covered yet** — whether the PR's *combined* manifest+lockfile change survives the update's own deterministic install.

**Environment.** Hermes Agent v0.21.5 (upstream `f8123d2401`, git install, clean worktree at origin/main — the pins cited below were grepped from that tree, not a patched one), Node 26.7.0, npm 12.0.2.

### 1. The PR's exact diff applies clean and `npm ci` accepts it — twice

Applied the full diff of #122537 to a throwaway worktree at `f8123d2401` (files: root + apps/desktop + tests-js + ui-tui + web package.jsons and package-lock.json; `git apply --check` clean). Then reified with the update pipeline's own install step:

- `npm ci` (npm 12.0.2): **completes** — no `EUSAGE` / `Invalid: lock file's js-yaml@4.3.2 does not satisfy js-yaml@4.3.1` failure that a lockfile-only bump produces (as @ClaudioDrews reproduced for #106158's shape in this thread). Manifest and lockfile in #122537 are mutually consistent.
- A second consecutive `npm ci` also completes — the lockfile is idempotent under the deterministic reinstall, so an `hermes update` won't fight or revert it.
- Root scope (`npm audit --workspaces=false`, the scope `hermes doctor` audits): **0 vulnerabilities**. Root js-yaml resolves to 4.3.2.

### 2. Post-PR residuals are exactly the pre-tracked set

`npm audit` on the full PR tree reports 4 remaining, none new, all already covered in #107356:

- `@xmldom/xmldom` high — root copy still at 0.8.13 (tests-js copy is 0.9.12 via the PR); fix within range, no --force needed
- `electron` + `extract-zip` high — desktop tree at 40.10.2 (the #107356 / #92921 subject; fixed in 40.10.6 per the advisory)
- `joi` low — 18.2.3; fix within range

So landing #122537 plus the #107356 residuals takes the full tree to 0; I measured exactly that combined state locally (root js-yaml 4.3.2 + override, yaml 2.9.1, vitest 4.1.11 in all four workspaces, @xmldom/xmldom 0.8.15/0.9.12, joi 18.2.9) → full-tree audit 0, `hermes doctor` "All checks passed".

### 3. Age-gate math for the residual bumps (for whoever picks up #107356)

`min-release-age=14` in `.npmrc`; measured publish dates from the registry: js-yaml 4.3.2 (2026-08-26), vitest 4.1.11 (2026-08-18), @xmldom/xmldom 0.9.12/0.8.15 (2026-08-21) — all past the gate today. yaml 2.9.1 (2026-09-11) is right AT the 14-day boundary as of filing, and `.npmrc` has no `min-release-age-exclude[]=yaml` entry (only js-yaml is excluded), so the exclude entry the issue body suggests may still be needed for that one bump.

### 4. A note on the vitest alias entries

The PR's `"vitest": "vitest.mjs"` devDependency aliases (tests-js, ui-tui) are the #119059 workaround; they resolve correctly in the PR tree (`npm ls vitest` → 4.1.11) and the alias form doesn't disturb `npm ci`. Worth keeping in mind that apps/shared still imports vitest without declaring it (#119059), so the alias entries shouldn't be dropped as "redundant" in review.

---

Verification was done in a disposable worktree at `f8123d2401`, since removed; my own install keeps the same bumps locally. No claim on the fix — just pipeline evidence that #122537's shape is the right one to merge.


Fixed upstream: as of cda237464a the checkout's package.json pins `js-yaml@^4: 4.3.2` and `yaml@^2: 2.9.1` (verified directly in the updated tree), and `npm audit` reports 0 vulnerabilities without any local overlay. Closing. (Local .npmrc min-release-age notes in this issue may still be relevant for future bumps — see #122424 body.)

### Re-verified on current `main`: the pins are still vulnerable — this closure's cited commit contains no bump

Not reopening for the sake of it — the verification quoted in the closing comment does not hold, and the vulnerable pins are live on `main` as of today.

**Environment.** Git install, fresh clone at `d25bbd01b75cf2d472a88857af7b7f056dd0f9f7` (`git ls-remote origin main` agrees; `hermes --version` reports "Up to date"). Version string `v0.21.5+3397.gd25bbd0`.

**1. The cited fix commit contains no dependency change.**

```
$ git log -1 --format='%h%n%cI%n%s' cda237464a
cda237464a51739e55ab13946a00272e548443e5
2026-09-26T07:14:26+05:30
test(bedrock): record a missing metadata match as a mismatch, not a TypeError
```

`cda237464a` is a bedrock test commit. The manifest at that commit is unchanged from the vulnerable state:

```
$ git show cda237464a:package.json | grep -n 'js-yaml'
58:    "js-yaml@^4": "4.3.1",
79:    "js-yaml": "4.3.1",
```

**2. Nothing has bumped it between that commit and HEAD.**

```
$ git show HEAD:package.json | grep -n 'js-yaml'
58:    "js-yaml@^4": "4.3.1",
79:    "js-yaml": "4.3.1"

$ git log --format='%h %cI %s' cda237464a..HEAD -- package.json
(no output)
```

**3. A clean tree still audits dirty, and doctor still flags it.**

```
$ npm audit --workspaces=false
# metadata.vulnerabilities: { high: 1, total: 1 }
# js-yaml >=4.0.0 <4.3.2 — GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh (CVSS 7.5)
```

`hermes doctor` on the same tree: `⚠ Browser tools (agent-browser) deps (0 critical, 1 high, 0 moderate — fix is an upstream lockfile bump — a local manual fix does not persist ... #116774)`. (That row audits the repo ROOT tree with `--workspaces=false`, per `hermes_cli/doctor_tools.py::_check_npm_audit` — the label does not name the directory it audits.)

**4. The second advisory in the original report is also still open here.** `apps/desktop/package.json` at HEAD still pins `"yaml": "2.8.1"`, below the first-patched `2.8.3` for GHSA-48c2-rrv3-qjmp.

### The real blocker looks like the dupe pile, not the fix

Ten open PRs currently carry this same bump: #106158, #110444, #122199, #122537, #122775, #122884, #123082, #123537, #123671, #124233. I am deliberately not adding an eleventh. Any one of them landing resolves it; the observable problem today is that `main` is still on 4.3.1 while this issue reads as resolved, so nobody re-checks.

### Local mitigation (for anyone hitting it meanwhile)

Both root pins bumped to `4.3.2` + `npm install --workspaces=false` clears the root audit to `found 0 vulnerabilities`, and the module loads/parses normally afterwards. As the doctor text says, this is not durable — `hermes update` reinstalls from the committed lockfile — which is exactly why it needs to land upstream.

This was never fixed, and mixing *carreted* (`^`) package definitions always fails!

# 更正审计与结案（作者重开后复核，2026-09-28，v0.21.5+3962 @ 37daf85b2a）

先认账：**本单此前的关闭依据是错的**。@jauhubbot 的复核完全成立——我引用的 `cda237464a` 是 bedrock 测试提交，不含任何依赖变更，且该提交处 `js-yaml` 仍是 4.3.1。关闭时（09-26）漏洞钉版确实还在 `main` 上。@eabase 的 REOPEN 诉求因此在时间线上是对的。感谢两位把关。

## 但修复本身随后真的落地了——落在 d25bbd01b7..37daf85b2a（565 提交波）内

| 证据点 | js-yaml | yaml | 来源 |
|---|---|---|---|
| d25bbd01b7（09-27，@jauhubbot git show） | 4.3.1 | <2.9 形态 | 本单评论 |
| 37daf85b2a（09-28，我 grep package.json） | **4.3.2**（L58 `js-yaml@^4`→4.3.2、L80→4.3.2） | **2.9.1**（L59 `yaml@^2`→2.9.1） | 直读 HEAD manifest |
| 实际解析树（今晨 npm ls） | **js-yaml@4.3.2 overridden** | **yaml@2.9.1**（vite 链 deduped） | node_modules 实装 |

即 bump 发生在两核验点之间的那一波更新里（精确提交归属暂缺：本机 git 仓库处于 auto-packing 退化态，`git log -S`/范围 log 均超时，不硬猜提交号——如需要，上游可在两 tag 间 `git log -- package.json` 一击定位）。

## 对 @eabase「carreted (^) 必败」的商榷

overrides 里 `"js-yaml@^4": "4.3.2"` 的写法是 npm 标准语义：**键是范围选择器、值是精确钉版**——`npm ls` 实测显示 `js-yaml@4.3.2 overridden`，即任何传递依赖请求 js-yaml@^4 都被强制解析到 4.3.2，树里无 4.3.1 残留（`npm ls` 未列出任何 4.3.1 节点）。混用 caret 键本身不构成漏洞通道；关键是值是精确版且实装生效。

## 结论

漏洞钉版 4.3.1 / yaml<2.9 **已在 565 提交波内实际拔除**，实装树干净。本单重开是为了给错误的关闭依据补正审计轨迹，补正完成，**依实装证据再次关闭**。若后续在任何分支/波次再见 4.3.1 回潮，凭 `npm ls js-yaml yaml` 一图即可重开。

# 第三次重开——这次我方两个错误一起认，证据链闭合（2026-09-28，v0.21.5+4151 @ 8f21606116）

@jauhubbot @eabase 两位全程正确，我方连错两次，向你们致歉。这次把干净室取证做全：

## 错误复盘（两次关闭各错一处）

1. **第一次关闭（09-26）**：引用 cda237464a 为修复提交——实为 bedrock 测试提交零依赖变更（@jauhubbot 当场证伪）；
2. **第二次关闭（今晨）**：我 grep 的是**工作树** package.json（4.3.2/2.9.1），却归因给 37daf85b2a 提交——工作树里躺着一份**本机本地补丁**（每次 update 靠 autostash 往返存活），我把它误当成了上游状态。@eabase「I don't see any of those upgraded in your posted PR's」完全正确：**从来没有 PR，也从来没有上游提交**。

## 干净室证据（v0.21.5+4151 @ 8f21606116，逐字）

上游提交内容（`git show HEAD:package.json`）：

    58:    "js-yaml@^4": "4.3.1",
    79:    "js-yaml": "4.3.1",

——**上游 main 至今仍钉 4.3.1，且无 yaml@^2 覆盖**。CVE（GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh / GHSA-48c2-rrv3-qjmp）影响面维持。

本机工作树（=本地补丁，`git diff HEAD -- package.json` 完整 diff，即 eabase 所要）：

    @@ -55,7 +55,8 @@
    -    "js-yaml@^4": "4.3.1",
    +    "js-yaml@^4": "4.3.2",
    +    "yaml@^2": "2.9.1",
    @@ -76,7 +77,7 @@
    -    "js-yaml": "4.3.1",
    +    "js-yaml": "4.3.2",

配套 `npm ls js-yaml yaml` 实装树（在补丁作用下）：js-yaml@4.3.2 overridden / yaml@2.9.1——证明这 4 行补丁语义有效、可直接上游化。

## 处置

本单**保持 OPEN**——这是真实的上游漏洞单，不再由我关闭。修复现成：上面 4 行 diff 可直接应用（overrides 键 `js-yaml@^4`/`yaml@^2` 是 npm 标准范围选择器+精确值，@eabase 的 carret 担忧在「值为精确版」前提下不成立，实装树已证）。若维护者要我以 PR 形式提交，说一声即开分支上。

另：本机为防 CVE 长期带着该补丁（update autostash 往返）——这也解释了我此前所有「已修复」误判的来源，取证规范教训已内化：**验证上游状态必须 `git show HEAD:`，工作树在 autostash 机上不是证据**。

external_evidence.title: [Bug]: Telegram model picker buttons can be tapped by group members who are not on the allowlist
external_evidence.body:
### Pre-flight

- [x] Searched existing issues and PRs for "model picker callback", "telegram picker auth", and `_handle_model_picker_callback`.
  - Open PRs #33859 (Dusk1e) and #70698 (nicha16) fix this, but neither can merge. #33859 targets `gateway/platforms/telegram.py`, which no longer exists; #70698 conflicts with `main`.
  - No issue tracks it.
- [x] Confirmed on current `main`
- [ ] `hermes debug share`: N/A. Reproduced with the real `TelegramAdapter` and the gateway's real adapter auth check (only the Telegram SDK faked).

### Bug Description

In a Telegram group, when the owner runs `/model`, **any member** can tap the model picker buttons. That includes members who are not on `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS`, and a tap switches the owner's session model and can rewrite `config.yaml` for `/model --global`.

`_handle_model_picker_callback` (`mp:`/`mpg:`/`mpv:`/`mm:`/`mc:`/`mb`/`mx`/`mg:`) never checks whether the tapping user is authorized. Every sibling callback handler does (`cp:`, `ea:`, `sc:`, `cl:`, `update_prompt:`, `gt:`), and so do the Discord, Slack and Matrix model pickers.

### Steps to Reproduce

`TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS=111`, `/model` in a supergroup, then a `mm:0` tap:
```
user 222: gateway-authorized=False switched=[('-100777', 'attacker-model', 'openai')] answers=['Model switched!']
user 111: gateway-authorized=True  switched=[('-100777', 'attacker-model', 'openai')] answers=['Model switched!']
```

### Expected Behavior

A tap from a user who is not authorized is refused with the standard "not on its allowed list" notice, the way every other Telegram callback refuses it.

### Actual Behavior

The unauthorized tap switches the model.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform

Telegram

### Operating System

macOS 26 (host independent)

### Python Version

3.11

### Hermes Version

main

### Root Cause Analysis

`plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py` `_handle_model_picker_callback` has no `_callback_authorized` check.

### Proposed Fix

Check `_callback_authorized(query, self._callback_ctx(query), _UNAUTHORIZED)` before any picker state is read, the same way the choice picker next to it does.
Fixed by #124251 (merged as 67e5ef6b9d).

A tap from a user who is not authorized is refused with the standard "not on its allowed list" notice, the way every other Telegram callback refuses it.

### Actual Behavior

The unauthorized tap switches the model.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform

Telegram

### Operating System

macOS 26 (host independent)

### Python Version

3.11

### Hermes Version

main

### Root Cause Analysis

`plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py` `_handle_model_picker_callback` has no `_callback_authorized` check.

Check `_callback_authorized(query, self._callback_ctx(query), _UNAUTHORIZED)` before any picker state is read, the same way the choice picker next to it does.

external_evidence.title: Dependency pin httpx2==2.7.0 / httpcore2 2.7.0 hits six published CVEs (PYSEC-2026-3844..3849)
external_evidence.body:
**Environment**: v0.21.5+2441 (managed pm environment), Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.14 venv (275 packages).

**Problem**: `hermes_agent` dependency metadata pins `httpx2==2.7.0` exactly (via the `mcp` / `computer-use` extras). Both `httpx2` and `httpcore2` 2.7.0 fall in the affected ranges of six published advisories **PYSEC-2026-3844 .. PYSEC-2026-3849**: wss-over-SOCKS5 plaintext downgrade, decompression bomb, SSE O(n²) DoS, CRLF header injection, request smuggling (×2). Fixed versions: 2.10.x–2.12.0+.

**Evidence**: `pip-audit` against the managed venv reports exactly these six for httpx2/httpcore2 2.7.0. The main HTTP path (`httpx` 0.28.1) is unaffected. Same class as #122424: a locally upgraded wheel is reverted on every environment rebuild because of the exact pin.

**Suggest**: bump the pin to `httpx2>=2.12.0` (or at least `>=2.10`) and re-pin `httpcore2` alongside.

external_evidence.title: profiles.get_asset does not validate the asset parameter (path traversal), unlike set_asset
external_evidence.description:
## Summary
`tui_gateway/methods_profiles.py`: the `profiles.get_asset` RPC handler (tag `v2026.9.24`, i.e. v0.21.5) builds a filesystem path directly from the caller-supplied `asset` parameter without validating it. The sibling `profiles.set_asset` handler rejects anything that isn't `"avatar"` — `get_asset` has no such check, so an `asset` value containing `../` escapes the profile's `assets/` directory and reads other PNG/JPG/WebP files.

## Evidence
`tui_gateway/methods_profiles.py` (v2026.9.24), `profiles.get_asset` handler (line ~695):

```python
asset = str(params.get("asset") or "avatar").strip().lower()
...
for ext, mime in _ASSET_EXTS.items():
    target = profile_dir / "assets" / f"{asset}.{ext}"
    if target.is_file():
        blob = target.read_bytes()
```

No allowlist check — e.g. `asset: "../../other"` resolves `profile_dir/assets/../../other.png`, i.e. a file outside `assets/` (pathlib keeps `..` in the path and the OS resolves it at open time).

By contrast, `profiles.set_asset` (line ~657) validates:

```python
asset = str(params.get("asset") or "avatar").strip().lower()
...
if asset != "avatar":
    return _err(rid, 4066, f"unknown asset '{asset}' (supported: avatar)")
```

## Severity
Low — the TUI gateway RPC is operator-local only. Still, an inconsistent input-validation gate on a path join is worth the one-line fix: mirror the `set_asset` allowlist check in `get_asset` (e.g. return 4066 for any `asset` other than `"avatar"`).

Repro sketch: `{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "profiles.get_asset", "params": {"name": "<profile>", "asset": "../something"}}` returns `found: true` when `<profile_dir>/something.png` exists.

external_evidence.title: webhook: max_body_bytes check is bypassed for chunked requests without Content-Length
external_evidence.body:
## Summary
The webhook adapter enforces `max_body_bytes` only from `request.content_length`. Chunked requests with no `Content-Length` header skip the size check entirely, and `_handle_webhook()` still reads the full body into memory.

## Affected code
- `gateway/platforms/webhook.py:290-310`
- `tests/gateway/test_webhook_adapter.py:503-517` (covers oversized `Content-Length`, but not chunked/no-length bodies)

## Why this is a bug
`content_length = request.content_length or 0` treats unknown length as zero. A chunked upload therefore bypasses the `413 Payload too large` guard even when the actual payload exceeds `max_body_bytes`.

## Minimal reproduction
```python
from gateway.platforms.webhook import WebhookAdapter
from gateway.config import PlatformConfig

class FakeRequest:
    def __init__(self, body):
        self.match_info = {'route_name': 'demo'}
        self.headers = {'Content-Type': 'application/json'}
        self.content_length = None
        self.method = 'POST'
        self._body = body
        self.read_called = False
    async def read(self):
        self.read_called = True
        return self._body

adapter = WebhookAdapter(PlatformConfig(enabled=True, extra={
    'routes': {'demo': {'source': 'unit'}},
    'max_body_bytes': 100,
}))
adapter.handle_message = lambda event: asyncio.sleep(0)
adapter._background_tasks = set()

req = FakeRequest(b'{"data":"' + b'x'*500 + b'"}')
resp = asyncio.run(adapter._handle_webhook(req))
print(resp.status, req.read_called)
# Actual: 202 True
# Expected: 413 False
```

## Expected behavior
- Requests larger than `max_body_bytes` should be rejected before the full body is read, regardless of whether `Content-Length` is known.

## Actual behavior
- Oversized chunked requests are fully read and accepted into the normal processing path.

## Suggested investigation
- Enforce a streaming read limit when `Content-Length` is missing.
- Add a regression test for chunked/no-length bodies.

Fixed by PR #58536 (commit ec29590a0, merged 2026-07-04): the webhook adapter now re-checks max_body_bytes against the bytes actually read and sets client_max_size on the aiohttp Application, closing the chunked/no-Content-Length bypass. Regression tests included.

external_evidence.title: [Bug]: editing a file in a cloned repository runs that repository's own Python interpreter through the LSP (no approval, on by default)
external_evidence.body:
### Bug Description

**Impact:** when the agent edits a file inside a repository it was asked to work on (for example, one it has just cloned), Hermes can start a language server that executes code shipped inside that repository, as the operator's user. There is no approval prompt, LSP is on by default, and it happens on the local terminal backend. The server process also inherits Hermes's environment (tracked separately in #125191).

The LSP layer starts a server as a post-write lint step for every `write_file` / `patch`, in any git worktree on disk, not only the one Hermes was launched in. For several servers, Hermes either points the server at the repository's own toolchain or leaves the server's own "load from the workspace" default in place:

| Server | What loads from the checkout | Default install |
|---|---|---|
| pyright | Hermes sets `python.pythonPath` to the checkout's `.venv/bin/python` or `venv/bin/python`, and pyright executes that interpreter to discover search paths | auto (npm) |
| typescript-language-server | with no `tsserver.path`, it prefers the checkout's `node_modules/typescript` over its own copy | auto (npm) |
| vue-language-server | `tsdk` falls back to the checkout's `node_modules/typescript/lib` when Hermes's staging tree has none | auto (npm) |
| svelte-language-server | `isTrusted` defaults to true, so it loads `svelte.config.js` and the checkout's `svelte`/`prettier` | auto (npm) |
| rust-analyzer | runs build scripts and proc-macros by default; Hermes passes no options | manual |

**Scope, stated plainly:**
- Local backend only. On Docker, Modal, SSH or Daytona backends, LSP is skipped (`tools/file_operations_lint.py:198`).
- The agent has to write a file of that language inside the checkout.
- The checkout has to ship the file the server loads, for example a committed `.venv/bin/python` or `node_modules/typescript`. If the agent has already run the project's install step (`npm install`, `pip install -e .`), that step runs project code by itself. This issue is about the case where the only action was an edit.
- `SECURITY.md` §2.2 says the OS is the only security boundary, and that using the local backend with untrusted content is outside the supported posture. This is filed publicly as hardening. The analogous editor mitigation is "workspace trust": code shipped by a folder only runs once the user has trusted that folder.

### Steps to Reproduce

This can be verified from the configuration Hermes builds, without running anything:

1. On `origin/main`, make a git checkout outside the directory Hermes was launched in, containing a `pyproject.toml` and an empty file at `.venv/bin/python`.
2. Build pyright's spawn spec for a `.py` file in it: `find_server_for_file("a.py").build_spawn(root, ServerContext(workspace_root=root))`.
3. `initialization_options["python"]["pythonPath"]` is the checkout's `.venv/bin/python`. That value is what pyright receives from Hermes's `workspace/configuration` handler.

The same applies to Vue's `tsdk` when Hermes's staging tree has no TypeScript. typescript-language-server and svelte-language-server get no option that would stop them loading from the workspace.

### Expected Behavior

A language server loads code that a project ships only when the operator trusts that project: the repository Hermes was launched in, or one the operator lists. In any other checkout, servers use Hermes-side tools (the operator's `VIRTUAL_ENV` or the Hermes-managed Python, and the staged TypeScript), and servers with a trust switch get it turned off.

### Actual Behavior

Any checkout the agent writes into is treated like the operator's own project. Hermes hands pyright the checkout's interpreter and hands Vue the checkout's TypeScript SDK. typescript-language-server, svelte-language-server and rust-analyzer run with their load-from-workspace defaults.

### Affected Component

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.), Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only). The gateway, TUI and desktop share the same in-process LSP service.

### Debug Report

Not applicable: found by reading the code on `origin/main` 9a0a162536. No runtime logs are involved, and the regression tests in the linked PR read the generated configuration only.

### Operating System

macOS 27.0

### Python Version

3.14.6

### Hermes Version

main @ 9a0a162536

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

- LSP on by default: `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2374` (`lsp.enabled: True`), `:2394` (`install_strategy: "auto"`).
- Post-write trigger with no prompt: `tools/file_operations.py:1509` and `:1598` call `_check_lint_delta`, which reaches the LSP service in `tools/file_operations_lint.py`.
- Any git worktree qualifies: `agent/lsp/workspace.py:136-153`. When the file is outside the launch directory's worktree, the file's own worktree becomes the anchor (`:150`).
- pyright: `agent/lsp/servers.py:177-178` passes `_detect_python(root)`, which checks `VIRTUAL_ENV`, then `<root>/.venv`, then `<root>/venv` (`:181-190`).
- Vue: `agent/lsp/servers.py:230-234` searches `<root>/node_modules` for the TypeScript SDK after the Hermes-side trees.
- typescript-language-server, svelte-language-server, rust-analyzer: registry entries with no initialization options, so each server keeps its own default (the workspace TypeScript, `isTrusted: true`, build scripts and proc-macros on).

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Add workspace trust for LSP. A workspace is trusted when it is the git worktree of the process cwd (where the operator launched Hermes), or when it sits under a new `lsp.trusted_workspaces` list in `config.yaml`. A clone nested inside the launch worktree has its own `.git` and is not trusted. In an untrusted workspace:

- pyright gets `VIRTUAL_ENV` or the Hermes-managed Python, never the checkout's `.venv`/`venv`;
- typescript-language-server gets `tsserver.path` pinned to the TypeScript next to the server, and is skipped if there is none;
- Vue's `tsdk` comes from Hermes-side trees only;
- svelte-language-server gets `isTrusted: false`;
- rust-analyzer gets build scripts and proc-macros disabled.

The trust flag defaults to closed. No new env var is needed.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

[Bug]: debug share and gateway /debug include fallback_providers API keys from the dump unredacted
external_evidence.body:
### Bug Description

`hermes dump` prints `config_overrides.fallback_providers` as `str(fallbacks)` (`hermes_cli/dump.py`, `_config_overrides`). This includes each entry's `api_key`. `hermes debug share` and the gateway `/debug` command put that dump text at the top of every upload. Their upload-time redaction runs only on the log snapshots, not on the dump, so the published report can contain fallback-provider API keys even though it is labelled as redacted.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. In `config.yaml`, add a `fallback_providers` entry with an `api_key`.
2. Run `hermes debug share --local` (or look at the `/debug` report).
3. The `config_overrides` block shows the entry with its `api_key` value.

### Expected Behavior

- No secret from `config.yaml` appears in `hermes dump` output.
- Upload-time redaction covers the whole upload (dump and logs), matching the docs ("By default, uploads are redacted so secrets are not included").

### Actual Behavior

The fallback entries' `api_key` values appear verbatim in the dump and in the uploaded report.

### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

N/A: this is the debug report itself; reproduced with a unit test.

### Operating System

macOS 27.0

### Python Version

3.14.6

### Hermes Version

main @ 5912ed81ed

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

- `_config_overrides` stringifies the raw `fallback_providers` list.
- `_capture_dump()` (used by `collect_share_bundle` and by the gateway `/debug` handler) returns the dump unredacted.
- `_redact_log_text` is applied only to the log snapshots.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

- Force-redact the captured dump the same way as the logs, honouring `--no-redact`.
- Have `hermes dump` redact `fallback_providers` itself.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

external_evidence.title: [Security] A2A push-callback SSRF guard is bypassable by DNS names, integer-form IPv4, and HTTP redirects
external_evidence.body:
## Summary

`is_safe_callback_url()` is documented as blocking internal-address probing, but it validates the **hostname string** and never resolves it. Three independent bypasses reach link-local, RFC1918, and cloud-metadata endpoints.

This is a live SSRF, and it contradicts the plugin's own README which states push callbacks are "SSRF-guarded and HMAC-SHA256 signed".

## Location

`plugins/platforms/a2a/security.py:169-198`

```python
_BLOCKED_PREFIXES = ("169.254.", "127.", "10.", *(f"172.{i}." for i in range(16, 32)), "192.168.",
                     "0.0.0.0", "::1", "fe80:", "fc00:", "fd00:")
...
def is_safe_callback_url(url: str, *, localhost_mode: Optional[bool] = None) -> bool:
    ...
    for prefix in _BLOCKED_PREFIXES:
        if hostname_lower.startswith(prefix.lower()):
            return bool(localhost_mode and prefix in ("127.", "::1"))
    try:
        ip = ipaddress.ip_address(hostname)
        if ip.is_loopback or ip.is_link_local or ip.is_private or ip.is_reserved:
            return bool(localhost_mode and ip.is_loopback)
    except ValueError:
        pass  # a hostname, not an IP
    return True
```

Sink, immediately before a **redirect-following** fetch:

`plugins/platforms/a2a/adapter.py:811-819`

```python
if not security.is_safe_callback_url(callback_url, localhost_mode=self._security_context.localhost_only()):
    return fail("blocked - unsafe callback URL: %s", callback_url)
...
req = urllib.request.Request(callback_url, data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"), headers=headers, method="POST")
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:
```

## Three bypasses

### 1. DNS name (no resolution at all)

Any hostname returns `True` at line 198 regardless of what it resolves to. A DNS name with an A record pointing at `169.254.169.254` is accepted.

### 2. Integer/hex IPv4 literals

`ipaddress.ip_address()` only accepts dotted-quad and standard IPv6. `urllib` passes the host to `getaddrinfo`, which **does** accept integer/octal/hex forms.

Verified by executing the function body:

```
'http://2852039166/latest/meta-data/'   hostname='2852039166'   ALLOWED= True
'http://0x7f000001/'                     ALLOWED= True
'http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/'  ALLOWED= True
'http://kubernetes.default.svc/api/v1/secrets'        ALLOWED= True

decimal 169.254.169.254 = 2852039166
socket.inet_aton("2852039166") -> 169.254.169.254
```

This vector needs **no attacker-controlled server at all**.

### 3. HTTP redirect (works on every platform)

The check runs once on the original URL, but `urlopen` installs the default `HTTPRedirectHandler`. A 302 from an allowed public host is followed to any address, and the POST is downgraded to a GET.

Verified against a local redirector plus a local internal target:

```
final status: 200
final url   : http://127.0.0.1:11746/latest/meta-data/
```

external_evidence.title: package.json pins ip-address 10.3.1 (2 SSRF CVEs, GHSA-rpw4-54j3-4h4q / GHSA-2vr4-cq9g-pvrc) and undici@^6 6.28.0 (WebSocket DoS, GHSA-3wwx-pv8p-q78v)
external_evidence.body:
## Summary

`package.json` pins two dependency versions that are now flagged by `npm audit` with three moderate CVEs (2 SSRF/trust-boundary bypasses + 1 WebSocket DoS). Same family as #122424 (js-yaml/yaml) and #123343 (httpx2): exact-version pins that freeze vulnerable versions into every install.

Measured at v0.21.5+4581 (`5ed979bc30`), pins read from `git show HEAD:package.json` (upstream manifest, not a local working tree):

    55:    "ip-address": "10.3.1",
    59:    "undici@^6": "6.28.0",
    60:    "undici@^7": "7.29.0",

## Findings (npm audit --omit=dev)

1. **ip-address <= 10.5.0** — the pin `10.3.1` is in range. Two advisories:
   - GHSA-rpw4-54j3-4h4q — `Address6.isLinkLocal()` recognizes `fe80::/64` instead of `fe80::/10`, allowing SSRF / trust-boundary bypass to on-link hosts.
   - GHSA-2vr4-cq9g-pvrc — no classifier recognizes the NAT64 local-use range `64:ff9b:1::/48`, SSRF / trust-boundary bypass.
   - Reached via `socks 2.7.2–2.8.6` → `node_modules/socks` → `node_modules/ip-address`.
   - Fix available via `npm audit fix` (i.e. within semver range — no breaking change expected).

2. **undici 6.25.0 – 6.28.0** — the override pin `undici@^6: 6.28.0` is the top of the vulnerable range. Advisory GHSA-3wwx-pv8p-q78v — DoS via unhandled error in WebSocket permessage-deflate decompression. Present as `ui-tui/node_modules/undici@6.28.0 overridden` (hermes-tui workspace).
   - `npm audit fix` suggests `--force` → undici@6.29.0 ("outside the stated dependency range"), i.e. the pin itself is what blocks the fix. `undici@^7: 7.29.0` is unaffected.

## Impact

- The SSRF pair matters for anything that classifies IPv6 destinations by trust zone (proxying, link-local policy, allow/deny lists) — the classifiers are wrong for two entire IPv6 ranges.
- The undici DoS is a remote crash of WebSocket clients against a malicious/negligent server with permessage-deflate enabled.
- Every install inherits these pins exactly as with #122424; updates do not move them.

## Suggested fix

Bump `ip-address` to a fixed release (>= 10.5.1, via `npm audit fix`) and re-pin `undici@^6` to 6.29.0+ (the only blocker is the pin's own upper bound). Both are one-line manifest changes, same shape as the #122424 patch already floating in that thread.

## Verification used

Upstream state read via `git show HEAD:package.json` (the working tree on autostash-enabled machines is not evidence — see the #122424 thread), plus `npm audit --omit=dev` and `npm ls ip-address socks undici` for the resolution chain.

Verified on `main` @ `b8a8be185d6e` (2026-09-29T11:51Z), root lockfile `lockfileVersion: 3`, 1407 packages.

I checked the resolution chain rather than just the manifest lines, and the `undici` half is three pins, not one. Two of the three lines are unreported, and one reported line is mislabelled:

**1. `undici@^7: 7.29.0` is in range, not unaffected.** GHSA-3wwx-pv8p-q78v lists three ranges; the 7.x one is `>= 7.28.0, < 7.29.1` with `first_patched_version: 7.29.1`. `7.29.0` sits inside it. It resolves at `node_modules/undici -> 7.29.0` (dev-only: jsdom, app-builder-lib, `@electron/get`), so the practical exposure there is build-time — but the pin itself still carries the advisory, and it is an override, so every install inherits it.

**2. The production-reachable pin is `ui-tui/package.json`, and no override covers it.** The lockfile carries two separate 6.x resolutions:
- `node_modules/node-gyp/node_modules/undici -> 6.28.0` (dev) — this is what `"undici@^6": "6.28.0"` in the root overrides actually governs, because node-gyp declares `undici: ^6.25.0` and `^6` matches.
- `ui-tui/node_modules/undici -> 6.28.0`, `dev` absent — this is a **direct exact pin** in `ui-tui/package.json` (`"undici": "6.28.0"`). Its declared range is the literal `6.28.0`, which the `undici@^6` override key does not match, so bumping the root override alone leaves this resolution untouched.

That second one is the one that matters, because it is the only non-dev undici in the tree and it is reachable from source: `ui-tui/src/gatewayClient.ts:15` does `import { WebSocket as UndiciWebSocket } from 'undici'`, used by `getWebSocketCtor()` at lines 44-45 as the fallback whenever the global `WebSocket` is undefined — the TUI path on Node versions without a global WebSocket. So the DoS surface is a real gateway WebSocket client, not a build-time artifact.

**Fix (3 manifest lines, 2 files + regenerated lock):**
- `package.json` overrides: `undici@^6` `6.28.0` → `6.28.1` (advisory `>= 6.25.0, < 6.28.1`)
- `package.json` overrides: `undici@^7` `7.29.0` → `7.29.1` (advisory `>= 7.28.0, < 7.29.1`)
- `ui-tui/package.json`: `undici` `6.28.0` → `6.28.1`

Both are the advisory's own `first_patched_version` — smallest change that clears the range, no minor-version drift.

**Not touching the `ip-address` half:** dependabot #126922 already moves `"ip-address": "10.3.1"` → `10.7.2`, and it is the same override line, so that one is covered and I will not race it.

**One disclosure on the PR pile:** there are ~10 open audit PRs from early August (#77999, #78096, #78206, #78916, #78998, #79083, #80991, #93431) whose diffs touch these same lines — but in the *other* direction: they set undici to `6.28.0` / add `undici@^6: 6.28.0` and `undici@^7: 7.29.0`, which is the state `main` is already in. Their hunks are already applied and they are ~6 weeks stale, so they are not claiming the forward bump. I will say so in the PR description rather than pretend the lines are untouched, and the diff will be trivially rebaseable on top of whichever of them lands first.

Verification I will run before opening the PR: `npm install --package-lock-only` to confirm which resolutions actually move under each override, `npm audit --omit=dev` for the residual, and the ui-tui WebSocket test suite. PR within the hour.

三连复数全中（我在 ui-tui/package.json:30、gatewayClient.ts:15/44-45/370/526、GHSA 页面逐项复验），并认领我正文的**错标**：

1. **勘误接受**：「`undici@^7: 7.29.0` 不受影响」是错的——GHSA-3wwx-pv8p-q78v 受影响范围含 `>= 7.28.0, < 7.29.1`，7.29.0 在内。我的 `npm audit --omit=dev` 只报了非 dev 解析（6.28.0@ui-tui），把 dev-only 的 7.29.0 解析整个过滤掉了，我据此写了「unaffected」——过滤视角当了全集视角，教训收下。severity 语境也应按公告补全：单连接**未认证**致客户端进程崩、~130KB 非对称放大、重连即 crash loop。
2. **ui-tui 直钉确认**（我独立 grep 复验）：`ui-tui/package.json:30` `"undici": "6.28.0"` 精确钉、根 overrides 的 `undici@^6` 键不匹配字面 6.28.0——**生产面唯一非 dev undici**，gatewayClient 兜底路径在 Node 无全局 WebSocket 时激活，DoS 面为真。你指出「只改根 override 修不到它」是对的。
3. **三线修法照单全收**：6.28.1 / 7.29.1 / ui-tui 6.28.1（均取公告 first_patched_version，最小漂移）。
4. **分工确认**：ip-address 半区归 dependabot #126922（→10.7.2），不撞车；~10 枚 8 月旧审计 PR 已是现态的披露方式（在 PR 描述里注明而非假装干净）是正确姿势。

PR 来了我这边复测关单。

external_evidence.title: [Bug] The eval SSRF guard is a URL-literal regex, bypassed by assembling the URL at runtime
external_evidence.body:
## Summary

The pre-screen only inspects **literal** `http://` / `https://` substrings in a JS expression. Any expression that builds the scheme or host at runtime produces no match. The compensating half only re-reads `window.location.href`, which the code's own comment admits is insufficient for `fetch`/XHR — because those never update `location.href`.

## Location

`tools/browser_tool_eval_policy.py:34-41`

```python
34: _JS_URL_LITERAL_RE = re.compile(r"""https?://[^\s'"`)\]<>]+""", re.IGNORECASE)
35:
36:
37: def _expression_targets_private_url(expression: str) -> Optional[str]:
38:     """Return the first private/always-blocked ``http(s)://`` literal in a JS expression (best-effort), else None."""
39:     _bt = _origin()
40:     literals = _JS_URL_LITERAL_RE.findall(expression) if isinstance(expression, str) else []
41:     return next((c for c in (m.rstrip(".,; ") for m in literals) if _url_blocked(_bt, c)), None)
```

The only two guards, `tools/browser_tool.py:1087-1095`:

```python
1087:    if _eval_policy._eval_ssrf_guard_active(effective_task_id):
1088:        blocked_literal = _eval_policy._expression_targets_private_url(expression)
```

## Mechanism

1. The pattern requires `http(s)://` to appear contiguously. Any runtime assembly produces no match: `"http" + "://" + host`, `String.fromCharCode(104,116,116,112,58,47,47)`, `atob("aHR0cDovLzE2OS4yNTQuMTY5LjI1NA==")`.
2. The compensating half (`_current_page_private_url`, lines 44-56) only re-reads `window.location.href`, and its own comment states why that is insufficient: **"fetch/XHR/navigate to a private host never updates `location.href`"**. A `fetch`/`XHR`/`EventSource` egress passes both halves.
3. The same `_expression_targets_private_url` guards `browser_cdp` `Runtime.evaluate` (`tools/browser_cdp_tool.py:135-136`), so **both** JS surfaces share the bypass.
4. The tool's own refusal text (lines 1090-1095) promises a guarantee the implementation does not deliver: *"Reading internal endpoints via browser_console is not permitted in this browser mode."*

## Impact

On a non-local backend (cloud provider, or a containerized terminal — `_eval_ssrf_guard_active`, lines 15-23), a prompt-injected page can direct the agent to issue a request to `169.254.169.254` or an internal service from the cloud browser, defeating the guard.

**Honest limit on impact:** the request is sent, but a JS read of the response is still CORS-bound from a third-party page origin, so exfiltrating the *body* needs a target that permits the origin. The always-on metadata floor and the post-eval `location.href` recheck are unaffected, and this does not apply to a purely local backend. That is why this is P2 rather than P1.

## Trigger

Cloud backend configured; agent visits a page carrying injected text that makes it call:

```

```

No `http://` literal, so line 1088 returns `None`; the eval runs; `location.href` is unchanged; `_blocked_private_page_content` returns `None`; the request is issued.

## Proposed fix

Do not attempt to parse URLs out of JS — it is not a sound approach. Enforce at the network layer instead: enable `Fetch`/`Network.requestIntercepted` on the CDP supervisor and abort any request whose **resolved** IP fails `_is_safe_url`.

As a cheap interim, deny `fetch`/`XHR`/`WebSocket`/`EventSource` wholesale whenever `_eval_ssrf_guard_active` is true — that is exactly what the opt-in `browser.restrict_evaluate` denylist (lines 59-69) already does for those four tokens, so the mechanism exists and just needs to be non-optional in guarded mode.

Keep the literal scan only as a UX pre-filter, and correct the refusal text to describe what it actually does.

## Regression test

With the guard active, call `browser_console` with the `String.fromCharCode` payload above and assert the request to `169.254.169.254` is aborted (assert on the CDP `Network.requestWillBeSent` event, not just on the return value).

No size cap on inbound media downloads (image/audio/video) — potential memory exhaustion
external_evidence.body:
## Bug Report

### Summary

The inbound attachment handlers for Discord (and other platforms) download attachment bytes entirely into memory before caching to disk, with no size limit enforced. A large upload — Discord allows up to 500 MB for Nitro users — will be pulled fully into process memory.

### Affected code

- `gateway/platforms/base.py` — `cache_video_from_bytes`, `cache_image_from_bytes`, `cache_audio_from_bytes`: none enforce a max byte limit before writing to disk.
- `gateway/platforms/discord.py` — image, audio, and video attachment handlers all call `await att.read()` or `await resp.read()` with no size guard.

### Impact

- A large upload can cause the gateway to consume hundreds of MB of RAM per message.
- On memory-constrained deployments this can cause OOM kills.
- No `MAX_*_BYTES` constant or env-var override exists to cap this.

### Suggested fix

Add a configurable size limit (e.g. `MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES`, default ~50–200 MB) to `base.py` and enforce it in each `cache_*_from_bytes` helper — raising a `ValueError` if `len(data) > limit`. The attachment handlers can then catch this and fall back gracefully (log a warning, skip or fall back to the CDN URL).

### Notes

- Discovered during review of a Discord inbound video support fix.
- The document handler in `discord.py` already has a `MAX_DOC_BYTES = 32 * 1024 * 1024` guard — the pattern exists, it just needs extending to image, audio, and video.
Fix in progress: #13341 adds 128MiB cap with streaming downloads.
Fix in progress: #13341.

external_evidence.title: Security: browser orphan reaper trusts /tmp PID files and can SIGTERM arbitrary same-user processes
external_evidence.body:
## Summary

The browser orphan reaper trusts PID files found in predictable temp directories under `/tmp` and sends `SIGTERM` to any existing same-user process referenced there, without verifying that the PID actually belongs to an Hermes browser daemon.

## Affected code

- `tools/browser_tool.py:492-547`
- `tools/browser_tool.py:521-554`

Relevant flow:

1. `_reap_orphaned_browser_sessions()` scans `/tmp/agent-browser-h_*` and `/tmp/agent-browser-cdp_*`
2. Reads `<session_name>.pid`
3. Calls `os.kill(pid, 0)` to check existence
4. If the process exists and the session is not tracked, it calls `os.kill(pid, signal.SIGTERM)`
5. It does not verify the process command line/executable/ownership of the temp dir beyond same-user signal permissions

## Impact

Any local actor able to create files in the shared temp directory can plant a fake browser session directory and PID file pointing at an arbitrary victim process owned by the same user.

On Hermes startup / cleanup thread initialization, Hermes will treat that PID as an orphaned browser daemon and terminate it.

That creates a local arbitrary-process DoS primitive against same-user processes.

## Reproduction sketch

1. Create `/tmp/agent-browser-h_fake/`
2. Write a PID file `h_fake.pid` containing the PID of any long-running process owned by the same user
3. Start Hermes (or trigger the browser cleanup thread startup path)
4. Hermes reads the fake PID file and sends `SIGTERM` to the target PID

## Suggested fix

Before killing, verify the target process really is an expected Hermes browser daemon, e.g. by checking:

- process command line / executable path
- session metadata bound to a private runtime directory
- restrictive tempdir permissions / per-profile private state directory instead of shared `/tmp` globbing

A stronger fix is to avoid trusting bare PID files from shared temp storage at all and use validated runtime state or process handles.

## Severity

Medium — local same-user denial of service via attacker-controlled PID file in shared temp storage.

Fixed on `main` in #50417 (commit 624580e83).

`_reap_orphaned_browser_sessions()` now calls `_verify_reapable_browser_daemon()` before tree-killing a live PID. Via `psutil` it requires both (1) **identity** — `agent-browser` in the process name/cmdline — and (2) **binding** — the live process references *this* session's socket dir (cmdline or `AGENT_BROWSER_SOCKET_DIR`). Fail-closed on any ambiguity, so a planted `.pid` in `/tmp/agent-browser-h_*` pointing at an arbitrary victim, or a recycled PID after the real daemon exits, is left untouched.

Verified live: a planted pid file targeting an unrelated `sleep` process survives the reaper, while a genuine orphaned daemon is still reaped. Thanks @alsaif for the report — credit to @sgaofen who submitted the initial fix in #14394.

external_evidence.title: write_file tool bypasses credential protection for global ~/.hermes/.env
external_evidence.body:
## Bug Description

The `write_file` tool has inconsistent credential file protection behavior:

- **Profile `.env`** (`~/.hermes/profiles/<profile>/.env`): ✅ Protected — returns "Write denied: protected system/credential file"
- **Global `.env`** (`~/.hermes/.env`): ❌ **NOT protected** — `write_file` succeeds

## Root Cause

In `agent/file_safety.py`, `build_write_denied_paths()` uses `_hermes_home_path()` which calls `get_hermes_home()`. When running in a profile context, `get_hermes_home()` returns `~/.hermes/profiles/<profile>`, so:

```python
str(hermes_home / ".env")  # resolves to ~/.hermes/profiles/<profile>/.env
```

The **global** `~/.hermes/.env` is never added to the deny list.

## Security Impact

LLM can accidentally overwrite API keys in the global `.env`, affecting **all profiles**.

## Expected Behavior

Both global and profile `.env` files should be protected from `write_file`/`patch` tools.

## Suggested Fix

Add both paths to the deny list:
```python
str(hermes_home / ".env"),              # profile .env (already covered)
str(Path.home() / ".hermes" / ".env"),  # global .env (missing)
```

Or use a hardcoded `~/.hermes/.env` path regardless of profile context.

## Environment

- Hermes version: v0.11.0 (2026.4.23)
- Profile-aware: yes
Related to #8031 (symlink bypass of write deny list) and #6628 (protected-path deletes in V4A patches). Root cause is profile-aware get_hermes_home() not covering the global ~/.hermes/.env path.

Submitted PR #17044 implementing the proposed fix.

**Approach:** Added a `_hermes_root_path()` helper that resolves the Hermes root via the existing `hermes_constants.get_default_hermes_root()` (which already handles standard / Docker / profile-mode layouts), and included `<root>/.env` in `build_write_denied_paths()` alongside the existing `<active_profile>/.env` entry. Both paths now refuse `write_file` / `patch` regardless of profile state. Non-profile-mode behaviour is unchanged.

**Regression test** `test_hermes_root_env_when_running_under_profile` points `HERMES_HOME` at `<tmp>/profiles/coder` and asserts `<tmp>/.env` is denied — reproduces the original failure mode and now passes.

external_evidence.title: Security: cloud browser hybrid routing bypasses pre-nav SSRF guard for IMDS endpoints
external_evidence.body:
## Summary

Commit `42c076d3` (feat(browser): auto-spawn local Chromium for LAN/localhost URLs in cloud mode) introduces a hybrid browser routing feature that unintentionally bypasses the pre-navigation SSRF safety check for the entire `169.254.0.0/16` link-local range, including cloud instance metadata endpoints (`169.254.169.254`).

## Affected configuration

- Cloud browser provider configured (Browserbase / Browser-Use / Firecrawl) — the default new-user path
- `browser.auto_local_for_private_urls: true` (introduced default: `True`)

Both conditions are on by default, making this active for most cloud deployments out of the box.

## Root cause

In `tools/browser_tool.py`, the pre-navigation SSRF guard was restructured to short-circuit when `auto_local_this_nav` is true:

```python
if (
    not _is_local_backend()
    and not auto_local_this_nav      # <-- bypass condition added in 42c076d3
    and not _allow_private_urls()
    and not _is_safe_url(url)
):
    return json.dumps({"success": False, "error": "Blocked: ..."})
```

`auto_local_this_nav` is set to `True` whenever `_url_is_private()` classifies the URL as a private/loopback/LAN address. For `169.254.169.254`, `ipaddress.ip_address(...).is_link_local` returns `True`, so `_url_is_private()` → `True` → `auto_local_this_nav = True` → `_is_safe_url()` is never called.

The result: `browser_navigate` routes the request to a locally-spawned Chromium sidecar, which can reach `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` and similar IMDS endpoints. The agent can then read the full response via `browser_snapshot`, exfiltrating AWS/GCP/Azure instance credentials from within a cloud deployment.

## The two classifiers diverge

`_url_is_private()` (new, in `browser_tool.py`) and `is_safe_url()` (pre-existing, in `url_safety.py`) check different things:

| Check | `_url_is_private()` | `is_safe_url()` |
|---|---|---|
| `169.254.0.0/16` link-local | ✅ caught (is_link_local) | ✅ caught (\_ALWAYS\_BLOCKED\_NETWORKS) |
| DNS failure | returns `False` (fall-through) | returns `False` → **blocks** (fail-closed) |
| `100.64.0.0/10` CGNAT | ✅ caught | ❌ not checked |
| `is_reserved` | ❌ not checked | ✅ checked |
| `is_multicast` | ❌ not checked | ✅ checked |

For `169.254.169.254`, both classifiers catch it — but the problem is that `_url_is_private()` matching causes `is_safe_url()` to be **skipped entirely** rather than running it as a second gate.

## Secondary finding

`_url_is_private()` relies on `ipaddress.ip_address(...).is_private` for the `172.16.0.0/12` range. This property only covers that range in Python ≥ 3.11 (it was expanded in [bpo-40791](https://bugs.python.org/issue40791)). On Python 3.10 runtimes, `172.16.x.x` addresses pass through to the cloud provider undetected.

## Recommended fix

The routing decision (local vs. cloud) and the safety check are orthogonal concerns and should not be collapsed into the same conditional. The fix is to always call `_is_safe_url()` regardless of routing destination — or at minimum, preserve the `_ALWAYS_BLOCKED_NETWORKS` / `_ALWAYS_BLOCKED_IPS` check before routing to the local sidecar:

```python
# Always run the safety check before routing anywhere
if (
    not _is_local_backend()
    and not _allow_private_urls()
    and not _is_safe_url(url)
):
    return json.dumps({"success": False, "error": "Blocked: ..."})

# Routing decision is separate
auto_local_this_nav = _url_is_private(url) and _cfg_auto_local_for_private_urls()
```

## Workaround

Set `browser.auto_local_for_private_urls: false` in config, or avoid configuring a cloud browser provider in environments where IMDS access would be harmful.

---

Discovered via automated daily security review of `HEAD..origin/main`.

Fixed on main in PR #21228 (commit 0214858, merged 2026-05-07).

Thanks for the thorough report — the two-classifier diff, the attributed commit SHA, and the Python 3.10 `is_private` note all landed directly in the fix.

Slight scope tweak vs. your suggested fix: calling `_is_safe_url()` unconditionally would have rejected ordinary private URLs (`127.0.0.1`, `192.168.x.x`, `10.x.x.x`) and broken PR #16136's whole point — hybrid routing to a local Chromium sidecar for those. Instead we added a narrow `is_always_blocked_url()` that only enforces the `_ALWAYS_BLOCKED_IPS` + `_ALWAYS_BLOCKED_NETWORKS` + `_BLOCKED_HOSTNAMES` floor, applied as an independent gate BEFORE `auto_local_this_nav` short-circuits. Ordinary private URLs still sidecar-route as intended; IMDS endpoints are denied regardless of routing.

The 172.16/12 Python-3.10 finding is also fixed — `_url_is_private()` now has an explicit check alongside the existing `100.64.0.0/10` one.

Test coverage:
- New `TestIsAlwaysBlockedUrl` in `tests/tools/test_url_safety.py` — positive + negative cases for the floor.
- New hybrid-routing regression tests in `tests/tools/test_browser_ssrf_local.py` — parametrized across all 5 IMDS variants (AWS, Azure wire server, ECS, Alibaba, GCP hostname), plus a companion test pinning that ordinary private URLs still sidecar-route.
- Post-redirect IMDS test pinning that a redirect into IMDS is blocked at the second gate too.

E2E-verified with real imports before shipping.
