Confirming this in production, with a live capture of the ignition — hopefully enough to clear `needs-repro`.

## Setup

`v0.19.1 (2026.7.30)` / `cc4cab2f`, Docker, one multiplex gateway hosting three entry profiles. Each profile's own `.env` pins `HERMES_KANBAN_BOARD` to its own board — all three pins are correct and none mentions another's board. Nothing else defines that key: verified absent from the image env / compose `environment:`, no `env_file` is declared, and no `config.yaml` has it as a top-level key.

## Symptom

Two of the three entries could not create kanban cards at all; the third worked normally. The failing entries resolved to the third profile's board — i.e. the value could only have come from that profile's `.env`, yet nothing in the documented configuration surface put it in the process environment.

## Why it stayed invisible

The loader leaves no trace. We swept the only two call sites that *do* leave one — `cli.py`, reachable from the slash-confirm "always" handlers, which both log a line and persist an `approvals.*` key — and got **zero log hits and no persisted key** across the whole process lifetime. That ruled those two out and left nothing else to follow. Three read-only investigation rounds could not localise it.

## Live capture

We backported the guard to our release at the same boundary this PR guards, and added a one-time-per-home `WARNING` at the skip point. On the **first agent turn after the restart**:

```
2026-08-03 12:24:50 UTC  skipped process-global .env load for
                         home=<data-root>/profiles/<entry-b> (multiplex active)
```

Seconds later that entry created its card on its own board, and the completion was delivered by that profile's own bot. Two things follow from the captured line:

1. **The carrier is an ordinary agent turn**, not an exotic path — no dashboard, no cron, no slash command involved.
2. **`hermes_home` was passed explicitly.** Our log prints the argument when present and a `<env-resolved>` sentinel otherwise; it printed a concrete path. That excludes the no-argument callers (`tools/mcp_tool.py:4607`, `hermes_cli/mcp_config.py:272`, `hermes_cli/main.py:691`) and points at the module-level loaders. `run_agent.py:128` is the most likely, which matches `env_loader.py`'s own docstring:

   > `load_hermes_dotenv()` runs at import time from several hot modules (cli.py, hermes_cli/main.py, run_agent.py, trajectory_compressor.py, ...)

   That docstring belongs to the `_APPLIED_HOMES` guard — which protects the secret-source *status lines* from printing 3-5x, but not `os.environ` itself. The repeated import-time invocation was known; only its effect on the shared environment was not.

## first-load-wins, confirmed by accident

Before the guard, whichever profile's turn ran first after a restart owned the process environment. Our restart happened to be followed by a turn from a *different* entry than the one that usually goes first. Had we restarted **without** the guard, that entry's own gate would have passed (env == its own pin) and our delivery test would have gone **green**, while the other two entries were silently broken — with no log anywhere to say so. The failure is symmetric; the winner is simply whoever is scheduled first.

Worth flagging because it makes the bug easy to misdiagnose as "works for me".

## On the fix

The choke-point placement in this PR is the right call — we independently landed on the same boundary, and it covers `cron/scheduler.py:3140` (same function, no guard, would load a whole profile `.env` including credentials during job execution) in one move. Two notes:

- `hydrate_profile_secret_sources()` does not exist in our release, so our backport simply returns `[]`. That is only equivalent because we have **no `secrets:` section configured** — deployments with external sources need this PR, not a naive backport of the early return.
- **Please consider keeping a log line at the skip point.** Without one this class of bug is undiagnosable after the fact: the mutation is silent, `/proc/<pid>/environ` only reflects process start, and nothing persists. A one-time-per-home `warning`/`info` costs nothing and converts "cannot reproduce" into a timestamp plus the offending home — it is what finally identified the carrier here after three rounds of failing to.

Happy to run anything else against this deployment.

external_evidence.title: Multiplexed gateway: profile-scoped .env load overwrites process-global os.environ, clobbering other profiles' adapter config mid-turn
external_evidence.description:
### Bug Description

Under `gateway.multiplex_profiles`, a profile-scoped `load_hermes_dotenv()` call overwrites **process-global** `os.environ`, so one profile taking a turn silently rewrites shared adapter config for every other profile served by the same gateway.

One multiplexed gateway process serves every profile, so `os.environ` is shared by all of their adapters. `hermes_cli/env_loader.py::load_hermes_dotenv()` writes the resolved home's `.env` into `os.environ` with `override=True`. Agent turns run in-process under a per-profile scope, so any module imported **lazily during a turn** re-runs its import-time loader call, resolves the home to the *routed* profile through the context-local override, and clobbers the shared values.

The result is a config that is correct at startup and wrong minutes later, with nothing logged. It reads as an intermittent platform fault.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a gateway with `gateway.multiplex_profiles: true` and at least two profiles that both connect Discord bots.
2. Put a **different** `DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS` in each profile's `.env` (e.g. root `.env` lists all 17 channels, `profiles/b/.env` lists only b's 5).
3. Start the gateway — the allowlist is correct (17 channels), and every bot answers in its own channels.
4. Send a message in a channel routed to profile B and let it run a **long** turn, long enough to pull in a lazily imported module (`trajectory_compressor` was the trigger here).
5. Now use a channel belonging to any other profile.

Minimal in-process repro, no Discord needed:

```python
secret_scope.set_multiplex_active(False)
env_loader.load_hermes_dotenv(hermes_home=default_home)   # startup
assert os.environ["SHARED_KEY"] == "all-channels"

secret_scope.set_multiplex_active(True)                    # gateway is multiplexing
token = hermes_constants.set_hermes_home_override(profile_home)   # turn routed to profile A
env_loader.load_hermes_dotenv(hermes_home=profile_home)    # lazy import mid-turn
hermes_constants.reset_hermes_home_override(token)

assert os.environ["SHARED_KEY"] == "all-channels"          # FAILS: "profile-a-only"
```

### Expected Behavior

A turn routed to one profile leaves the other profiles' adapter config alone. Profile credentials reach adapters through the isolated per-profile secret scope, which is the documented multiplex design.

### Actual Behavior

`os.environ` process-wide takes the routed profile's values. Concretely, on a 5-bot Discord gateway:

- startup: `DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS` = all 17 channels, every bot works;
- a few minutes after each restart it collapses to one profile's 5 channels;
- the other bots then reject slash commands in their own channels (`Unauthorized slash attempt ... reason='channel not in DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS'`) and **silently drop** plain messages — the allowlist gate returns before any inbound logging.

Every rejection in our logs directly followed a turn in the other profile's channel. Because each restart looked healthy, three separate fixes appeared to work and then "regressed".

Any value that is process-global but present in more than one profile `.env` can be affected; `DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS` is just where it was visible.

### Affected Component

Gateway (multiplex) / CLI env loading — `hermes_cli/env_loader.py`, surfacing through platform adapters.

### Messaging Platform

Discord (the mechanism is platform-independent).

### Operating System

Ubuntu (Linux 6.8), systemd user service.

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

v0.19.1 (2026.7.30) · git install. Code path is unchanged on current `main`.

### Root Cause Analysis

`load_hermes_dotenv()` treats `os.environ` as the destination for whichever home it resolves. That is correct for a single-profile process, but under multiplex the home is context-local (`hermes_constants.get_hermes_home_override()`) while `os.environ` is not — so a context-local read drives a process-global write. Any lazily imported module gives that write a trigger long after startup.

### Proposed Fix

When `agent.secret_scope.is_multiplex_active()` **and** a profile-home override is in scope, skip the global-env mutation entirely and return no applied paths. Startup loading (multiplex on, no scope installed yet) and single-profile gateways keep their existing behaviour.

PR with three regression tests: the clobber case fails on stock code with exactly this signature, and the two guard-rail cases pin the behaviour that must not change.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

Yes — submitted alongside this issue.


--- Issue comments ---
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Duplicate of #77562 — it reports the same turn-scoped `load_hermes_dotenv()` process-environment clobber under multiplexing.

Reviewed against current `origin/main` (dbb6acd333a) in the multiplexed-gateway backlog sweep.

Closing as a duplicate of #77562 (same author-confirmed root cause: a turn-scoped `load_hermes_dotenv()` writing the routed profile's `.env` into process-global `os.environ` with `override=True`). #77562 is the earlier report and the canonical tracking thread; the fix is riding #77592. Your companion PR #77970 is closed with credit for the regression tests, which are being ported into that salvage.

Nothing further needed here — if you have a repro that differs from #77562 (e.g. a loader call site other than the profile-scoped turn path), please add it there.

external_evidence.title: Root `overrides` pins brace-expansion to vulnerable 5.0.8, making `npm audit fix` a no-op (GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895)
external_evidence.body:
### Summary

The root `package.json` pins `brace-expansion` to `5.0.8` via `overrides`:

```json
"overrides": {
  "lodash": "4.18.1",
  "yauzl": "^3.3.1",
  "protobufjs": "^8.7.1",
  "brace-expansion": "5.0.8"
}
```

`brace-expansion` 5.0.8 is affected by GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895 (high — DoS via unbounded intermediate arrays, bypassing the CVE-2026-14257 mitigation). The fixed release `5.0.9` is published, but because the override hard-pins `5.0.8`, `npm audit fix` reports "fix available" and then does nothing ("up to date"), and `hermes doctor --fix` can't resolve it either. Every install permanently reports 2 high advisories through `minimatch` (via `@electron/asar`, `@electron/universal`, `dir-compare`, `filelist`, `glob`).

### Repro

On a git install of v0.20.0 (2026.8.3):

```
cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent
npm audit          # 2 high: brace-expansion 4.0.0 - 5.0.8
npm audit fix      # "up to date" — no change, override pins 5.0.8
```

### Suggested fix

Change the override to `"brace-expansion": "^5.0.9"` (or `5.0.9` if the exact pin was intentional for reproducibility) and refresh the lockfile. Users on git installs can't patch this locally without dirtying the repo and breaking `hermes update`.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3), install method: git
- macOS (Darwin 25.6.0), Node per engines >=22.22.0

Related but distinct from #68736 / #73426, which cover the web/ and ui-tui workspace dependency locks — this one is the root `overrides` pin blocking the documented remediation path.

Confirmed on Linux (Debian/Ubuntu, Hermes Agent v0.20.0, git install) — same behavior: npm audit shows 2 high (brace-expansion 4.0.0 - 5.0.8), npm audit fix reports "up to date" with no change because the override hard-pins 5.0.8.

Local workaround that worked for me without dirtying anything permanent (re-applies after hermes update): bash sed -i 's/"brace-expansion": "5.0.8"/"brace-expansion": "5.0.9"/' package.json npm install npm audit # → 0 vulnerabilities

After this, hermes doctor --fix passes clean. Would be great to see ^5.0.9 in the override upstream.

Adjacent to the `overrides` pin, there's a second stale artifact for the same package — the `.npmrc` cooldown exclusion, whose justifying comment is now factually void:

```ini
# .npmrc:34-35
# brace-expansion 5.0.8 includes fixes for vulns. remove this when 5.0.8 is > 2wks  old
min-release-age-exclude[]=brace-expansion
```

The premise ("5.0.8 includes fixes for vulns") was true of the earlier CVE-2026-14257, but GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895 (published 2026-08-03) explicitly bypasses that mitigation and its range is `>= 4.0.0, < 5.0.9` — so **5.0.8 is now itself the vulnerable version**, and the comment recommends removing the exclusion on the strength of a fix that no longer holds.

**The sequencing matters, because the two dates are in the wrong order:**

| version | published | exits 14d cooldown |
|---|---|---|
| 5.0.8 (pinned, vulnerable) | 2026-07-23 | 2026-08-06 |
| 5.0.9 (fixed) | 2026-07-30 | **2026-08-13** |

Following the comment literally removes the exclusion on ~2026-08-06, which is **7 days before 5.0.9 can satisfy `min-release-age=14`**. Between those dates the exclusion is load-bearing: drop it early and the fixed version is unreachable, reproducing exactly the ETARGET failure documented in #78893.

So the exclusion probably wants to be *retained* through the `^5.0.9` bump suggested above and removed on/after 2026-08-13 — the opposite of what the comment currently instructs.

More generally, these exclusions are the soft spot in the #50901 cooldown: each one permanently exempts a package name from the age gate, and they're carrying justifications that expire silently. Given that same-day-published packages with valid provenance are the live threat model (the 2026-08-04 keyv/cacheable worm), it may be worth giving each `min-release-age-exclude[]` entry an explicit expiry date and a CI check that fails when one is past it — so a stale exemption surfaces as a build signal rather than sitting in a comment.

Verified on v0.20.0 (2026.8.3) `3c27eb6`, git install, macOS; `node_modules/brace-expansion` resolves to 5.0.8.

Confirming this independently on **v0.20.0 (2026.8.3)**, git installs, on two machines (macOS 26 arm64, npm 10.9.8; Linux server, npm 10.9.4). Same behaviour: `npm audit fix` reports a fix and then does nothing, and `hermes doctor --fix` does not touch these advisories either — it only lists them.

Two additions to the diagnosis, in case they help whoever picks this up:

**The `undici` half has the same shape but a different mechanism.** `brace-expansion` is pinned by the root `overrides`; `undici` is pinned by an exact version in `ui-tui/package.json` (`"undici": "6.27.0"`), with the transitive copies coming from `node-gyp` (via electron-builder) and `jsdom` (via vitest). So the three groups `hermes doctor` reports are really the same two packages in build-tool chains, and both need a manifest edit rather than `npm audit fix`.

**Patching in place needs a second step.** Editing the manifests is not enough on an existing checkout — `npm install` leaves the already-installed nested copies and only marks them:

```
undici@6.27.0 invalid: "^6.28.0" from node_modules/node-gyp overridden
undici@7.28.0 invalid: "^7.29.0" from node_modules/jsdom overridden
```

`npm update undici --include-workspace-root --workspaces` is what actually resolves them; after that all three audit targets report zero vulnerabilities.

#79184 already carries these manifest bumps plus the `.npmrc` `min-release-age-exclude[]=undici` line, which the manifest-only PRs (#77967, #78353, #78998) lack — that exclusion matters on npm ≥ 11.6, since both fixes are still inside the 14-day window (`undici` 6.28.0/7.29.0 published 2026-07-24, `brace-expansion` 5.0.9 on 2026-07-30). Verified both my local fix and that PR's changes produce a clean audit, so from my side this issue is fully addressed by #79184.

Verified on https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/be59f0411e8fffa1e6f48425f7885c5c6badb705: root overrides pin brace-expansion 5.0.9 and undici 6.28.0 / 7.29.0. Fixed by https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/7537de9e74940f0f954438138bd87dacb9969751.

Confirmed on Linux (Debian/Ubuntu, Hermes Agent v0.20.0, git install) — same behavior: npm audit shows 2 high (brace-expansion 4.0.0 - 5.0.8), npm audit fix reports "up to date" with no change because the override hard-pins 5.0.8.

Local workaround that worked for me without dirtying anything permanent (re-applies after hermes update): bash sed -i 's/"brace-expansion": "5.0.8"/"brace-expansion": "5.0.9"/' package.json npm install npm audit # → 0 vulnerabilities

After this, hermes doctor --fix passes clean. Would be great to see ^5.0.9 in the override upstream.

Adjacent to the `overrides` pin, there's a second stale artifact for the same package — the `.npmrc` cooldown exclusion, whose justifying comment is now factually void:

```ini
# .npmrc:34-35
# brace-expansion 5.0.8 includes fixes for vulns. remove this when 5.0.8 is > 2wks  old
min-release-age-exclude[]=brace-expansion
```

The premise ("5.0.8 includes fixes for vulns") was true of the earlier CVE-2026-14257, but GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895 (published 2026-08-03) explicitly bypasses that mitigation and its range is `>= 4.0.0, < 5.0.9` — so **5.0.8 is now itself the vulnerable version**, and the comment recommends removing the exclusion on the strength of a fix that no longer holds.

**The sequencing matters, because the two dates are in the wrong order:**

| version | published | exits 14d cooldown |
|---|---|---|
| 5.0.8 (pinned, vulnerable) | 2026-07-23 | 2026-08-06 |
| 5.0.9 (fixed) | 2026-07-30 | **2026-08-13** |

Following the comment literally removes the exclusion on ~2026-08-06, which is **7 days before 5.0.9 can satisfy `min-release-age=14`**. Between those dates the exclusion is load-bearing: drop it early and the fixed version is unreachable, reproducing exactly the ETARGET failure documented in #78893.

So the exclusion probably wants to be *retained* through the `^5.0.9` bump suggested above and removed on/after 2026-08-13 — the opposite of what the comment currently instructs.

More generally, these exclusions are the soft spot in the #50901 cooldown: each one permanently exempts a package name from the age gate, and they're carrying justifications that expire silently. Given that same-day-published packages with valid provenance are the live threat model (the 2026-08-04 keyv/cacheable worm), it may be worth giving each `min-release-age-exclude[]` entry an explicit expiry date and a CI check that fails when one is past it — so a stale exemption surfaces as a build signal rather than sitting in a comment.

Verified on v0.20.0 (2026.8.3) `3c27eb6`, git install, macOS; `node_modules/brace-expansion` resolves to 5.0.8.


Confirming this independently on **v0.20.0 (2026.8.3)**, git installs, on two machines (macOS 26 arm64, npm 10.9.8; Linux server, npm 10.9.4). Same behaviour: `npm audit fix` reports a fix and then does nothing, and `hermes doctor --fix` does not touch these advisories either — it only lists them.

Two additions to the diagnosis, in case they help whoever picks this up:

**The `undici` half has the same shape but a different mechanism.** `brace-expansion` is pinned by the root `overrides`; `undici` is pinned by an exact version in `ui-tui/package.json` (`"undici": "6.27.0"`), with the transitive copies coming from `node-gyp` (via electron-builder) and `jsdom` (via vitest). So the three groups `hermes doctor` reports are really the same two packages in build-tool chains, and both need a manifest edit rather than `npm audit fix`.

**Patching in place needs a second step.** Editing the manifests is not enough on an existing checkout — `npm install` leaves the already-installed nested copies and only marks them:

```
undici@6.27.0 invalid: "^6.28.0" from node_modules/node-gyp overridden
undici@7.28.0 invalid: "^7.29.0" from node_modules/jsdom overridden
```

`npm update undici --include-workspace-root --workspaces` is what actually resolves them; after that all three audit targets report zero vulnerabilities.

#79184 already carries these manifest bumps plus the `.npmrc` `min-release-age-exclude[]=undici` line, which the manifest-only PRs (#77967, #78353, #78998) lack — that exclusion matters on npm ≥ 11.6, since both fixes are still inside the 14-day window (`undici` 6.28.0/7.29.0 published 2026-07-24, `brace-expansion` 5.0.9 on 2026-07-30). Verified both my local fix and that PR's changes produce a clean audit, so from my side this issue is fully addressed by #79184.


Verified on https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/be59f0411e8fffa1e6f48425f7885c5c6badb705: root overrides pin brace-expansion 5.0.9 and undici 6.28.0 / 7.29.0. Fixed by https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/7537de9e74940f0f954438138bd87dacb9969751.

external_evidence.title: [Bug]: redact — dotted sk-sp- keys (Alibaba Token Plan) leak past the sk- prefix pattern on the code_file path
external_evidence.body:
## Bug Description

`agent/redact.py` `_PREFIX_PATTERNS` line 73:

```python
r"sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}",           # OpenAI / OpenRouter / Anthropic (sk-ant-*)
```

The character class excludes `.`, so a key whose body contains dots is only
matched **up to the first dot**. The remainder passes through unmasked.

Alibaba Cloud **Token Plan** (savings-plan) API keys are exactly this shape:
`sk-sp-<segment>.<segment>.<segment>` (110+ chars, several dots). On the
default terminal-output path this leaks most of the key in cleartext.

This is the same bug class as #58167 (SendGrid pattern masking only the
key-id segment while the key-secret stays in cleartext): a pattern that
matches a *prefix of the credential* is worse than no pattern, because the
partial mask (`sk-sp-...xxxx`) reads as "redacted" while the tail is live.

## Steps to Reproduce

All keys below are **fake**. Run against `agent/redact.py` on current main:

```python
from agent.redact import redact_terminal_output

FAKE_DOTTED = "sk-sp-f4k3t0k3n4t3std4t4.part2xyz.part3tail"  # dotted, fake
FAKE_PLAIN  = "sk-sp-f4k3t0k3n4t3std4t4xyz"                  # no dots, fake

# What `cat ~/.hermes/.env` (or grep) shows as tool output — the DEFAULT path:
print(redact_terminal_output(
    f"ALIBABA_CODING_PLAN_API_KEY={FAKE_DOTTED}", command="cat ~/.hermes/.env"))
print(redact_terminal_output(
    f"ALIBABA_CODING_PLAN_API_KEY={FAKE_PLAIN}",  command="cat ~/.hermes/.env"))
```

## Expected Behavior

Both values fully masked (or replaced with a non-reusable sentinel), e.g.
`ALIBABA_CODING_PLAN_API_KEY=sk-sp-...tail` or `«redacted:sk-…»`.

## Actual Behavior

```
ALIBABA_CODING_PLAN_API_KEY=sk-sp-...d4t4.part2xyz.part3tail   <- dotted: TAIL LEAKS
ALIBABA_CODING_PLAN_API_KEY=sk-sp-...4xyz                      <- no dots: masked fine
```

The dotted key is masked only up to the first dot; everything after it
(`.part2xyz.part3tail` here — ~half of a real key) survives into tool output.

### Why this specific path is the dangerous one

`redact_terminal_output` sets `code_file=True` for anything that is not an
env-dump command (`env`/`printenv`/`set`/`export`/`declare`) — so `cat`,
`grep`, `read_file` etc. all skip the `_ENV_ASSIGN_RE` pass that would
otherwise catch `NAME=<value>` pairs. On that path the prefix regex is the
only guard, and it partial-matches. For comparison, `command="env"`
(`code_file=False`) masks the whole value via `_ENV_ASSIGN_RE` — confirmed
in testing.

## Real-world impact

Reported after a real incident: a user's Alibaba Token Plan key (dotted
`sk-sp-` form) was printed by a `cat ~/.hermes/.env` during an active Hermes
session, persisted verbatim into `~/.hermes/state.db` (10 message rows), and
was shipped as conversation context to upstream providers. The key had to be
rotated and `state.db` checkpointed + VACUUMed to remove the residue. No
actual key material is included in this report.

## Proposed Fix

Add a dedicated dotted pattern **before** the generic `sk-` entry (alternation
order matters — leftmost alternative wins at the same position):

```python
_PREFIX_PATTERNS = [
    r"sk-sp-[A-Za-z0-9._-]{10,}",        # Alibaba Token Plan / savings-plan keys (dotted bodies)
    r"sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}",            # OpenAI / OpenRouter / Anthropic (sk-ant-*)
    ...
]
```

Precedent: the GitLab runner tokens already use dotted character classes for
the same reason (`glrt-`, `glrtr-` → `[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]`). The `_PREFIX_SUBSTRINGS`
pre-screen is derived automatically from `_PREFIX_PATTERNS`, so gating stays
false-negative-free with no other change needed.

Verified against fake keys: the dedicated pattern fully consumes dotted keys
(including URL-embedded and sentence-final-period cases, where the negative
lookahead correctly stops at the boundary), and the existing `sk-` behavior
for non-dotted keys is unchanged.

Optionally, the same dot could be added to the generic `sk-` class, but the
targeted `sk-sp-` entry is the lower-risk fix (broader class risks swallowing
sentence-final periods after ordinary `sk-` tokens).

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20), verified against `origin/main` @ `91937a6d`
  (`agent/redact.py` line 73 unchanged)
- macOS 26, Python 3.11
- Labels: `comp/agent`

external_evidence.title: [Security] Terminal tool fails to mask JWT-format API keys
external_evidence.description:
## Bug Description

The terminal tool's API key masking mechanism inconsistently redacts secrets. Keys in traditional format (e.g. `sk-xxxx`) are masked, but JWT-format keys (containing `.` separators, e.g. DashScope/Alibaba) are displayed in plaintext in chat output.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a provider with a JWT-format API key (e.g. `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY`)
2. Run a grep command against `.env` that outputs the key:
   ```bash
   grep -i "DASHSCOPE\|alibaba\|qwen" ~/.hermes/.env | grep -v "^#"
   ```
3. Observe the full API key is displayed unmasked in the terminal output

## Expected Behavior

All API keys should be masked regardless of format, including JWT-style tokens with `.` separators.

## Actual Behavior

- `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-ddf...ce70` — partially truncated ✓
- `XIAOMI_API_KEY=sk-c9t...l5ki` — partially truncated ✓
- `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY=sk-ws-H.EEPXREE.pFau.MEUCIQC6UnD-jj2a...` — fully visible ✗

## Root Cause Analysis (tentative)

The masking regex likely uses a pattern like `sk-[a-zA-Z0-9-]{N,}` which fails to match JWT keys because the `.` character breaks the continuous alphanumeric match, resulting in a match length below the detection threshold.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: latest (2026.9.9)
- OS: Windows 11
- Shell: bash (Git Bash / MSYS)

## Suggested Fix

Update the API key detection regex to handle JWT-format keys, or switch to a broader heuristic (e.g. match any `sk-*` prefix and mask until whitespace/end of line, regardless of character class).

--- Issue comments ---
## Root Cause (file:line evidence from current `origin/main`)

The terminal tool's secret redaction is controlled by **`agent/redact.py`**, specifically:

- **Line 44**: `_PREFIX_PATTERNS` = `r"sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}"` for vendor-prefix keys (OpenAI/DashScope/etc.)
- **Line 323**: `_JWT_RE` = `r"eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9_=-]{4,}){0,2}"` for JWTs

Both character classes forbid `.` (period) in the token body **before the first section-separator dot** (the `\.` in `_JWT_RE` is a **literal** boundary, not a body-allowed char). 

When a key contains `.` **embedded in its first segment** (like DashScope `sk-ws-H.EEPXREE.pFau.MEUCIQC...`), the pattern matches only up to the first unexpected `.`, leaving the remainder unmasked.

- `sk-ws-H` → matched (17 chars: `sk-` + 15 token chars)
- `.EEPXREE.pFau.MEUCIQC...` → **leaked verbatim** (the `.` after `H` breaks the contiguous `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` run)

## Fix (PR incoming within the hour)

Add `.` to the token-body classes in **both** patterns:

```diff
-    r"sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}",           # OpenAI / OpenRouter / Anthropic (sk-ant-*)
+    r"sk-[A-Za-z0-9._-]{10,}",          # OpenAI / OpenRouter / Anthropic / DashScope (embedded dots)
 
-_JWT_RE = re.compile(r"eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9_=-]{4,}){0,2}")
+_JWT_RE = re.compile(r"eyJ[A-Za-z0-9._-]{10,}(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9._=-]{4,}){0,2}")
```

The trailing quantifier `{0,2}` already handles standard 3-part JWTs (header + payload + sig) — the `.` now allowed in each section lets non-standard dotted tokens pass through masked.

### Regression test plan
- Construct an API key `sk-test.dot.embedded.token` and verify it is fully masked by `_PREFIX_RE.sub(lambda m: _mask_token(m.group(1)), text)`
- Construct a synthetic JWT `eyJfake.part2.part3` with embedded dots and verify `_JWT_RE.sub(...)` masks it end-to-end
- Confirm pre-existing `sk-xxxNoDotsxxx` keys still mask correctly (no behavior change for traditional tokens)

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Duplicate of #78128 — same mechanism: the `sk-` prefix pattern in `agent/redact.py` uses a character class that excludes `.`, so dotted Alibaba/DashScope JWT-format keys stop matching at the first dot and pass through on the `code_file` terminal path. Fix candidates: #78490 (central dotted-continuation for all vendor prefixes) and #106520 (widens the `sk-` class).

external_evidence.title: Secret redaction misses dot-containing and non-sk- prefixed API keys
external_evidence.description:
### Summary

Two gaps in `agent/redact.py` let real API keys land in plaintext in session storage (and anywhere tool output is echoed or stored):

1. **`.` is not in the `sk-` character class.** The pattern `sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}` stops at the first dot, so vendor keys that embed a dot are only partially masked — everything after the first dot stays in plaintext.
2. **Keys without a known vendor prefix are never matched.** For example Zhipu (bigmodel.cn) keys look like `50aaed…ZpSh` and match no entry in `_PREFIX_PATTERNS`, so they pass through verbatim.

### Repro (v0.21.3, macOS, git install)

Write this file, then `cat` it through the terminal tool:

```yaml
a:
  api_key: sk-sp-ABCDEFGH1234567890.abcdefgh1234567890_XYZ-0987654321
b:
  api_key: 50aaedFAKE1234567890abcdef1234567890abc.ZpSh99
```

Observed output:

```
a:
  api_key: sk-sp-...7890.abcdefgh1234567890_XYZ-0987654321
b:
  api_key: 50aaedFAKE1234567890abcdef1234567890abc.ZpSh99
```

Expected: the full value masked in both cases.

### Root cause

- `_PREFIX_PATTERNS`: `r"sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}"` — the class lacks `.`, so the match ends at the first dot. Real-world Alibaba Bailian keys (`sk-sp-…`) embed a dot and are left mostly unmasked.
- Zhipu keys carry no `sk-` prefix and have no dedicated pattern.

### Impact

Keys stay in plaintext inside `state.db` message rows and are re-served verbatim by `session_search` and memory search, so the leak compounds across sessions. Since redaction here is a stated security boundary, worth closing both: include `.` in the class (or mask to end-of-token) and add the missing vendor prefixes.

Happy to send a patch if useful.


--- Issue comments ---
Consolidation pointer: the fix for this issue is being carried in #113908 (opened first; its `32–40`-char alnum ID shape masks the reporter's exact mixed-case repro, which a stricter 32-lowercase-hex variant does not — I checked both regexes against the repro side by side). My parallel attempt #113916 has been withdrawn in its favor, with two extra negative controls suggested there for the surviving carrier: benign 32-hex filenames / bare shas staying unmasked, and a `file_read` nonreusable-mask variant.

Adding a third instance of the same class — but this one is a *wrong-prefix* bug in a pattern that already exists, rather than a missing pattern.

## Case: Mem0 Platform keys are never matched by the pattern written for them

`agent/redact.py:173`:

```python
r"mem0_[A-Za-z0-9]{10,}",           # Mem0 Platform API key
```

Real Mem0 Platform keys are minted as `m0-…` (dash, no `mem0_` segment), so this entry is a no-op for every real key.

## Repro (v0.21.3, macOS, git install @ `77ecc72b`)

```python
from agent.redact import redact_sensitive_text

M0 = "m0-ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ123456"   # real format, fake value
controls = [
    M0,                                            # bare
    f"https://api.mem0.ai/?k={M0}",                # in a URL
    f"mem0 add failed (401): key={M0} rejected",   # in an error string
    f"Authorization: Token {M0}",                  # in a header
    f"MEM0_API_KEY={M0}",                          # env assignment
    "mem0_ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ",             # control: the format the pattern expects
]
for s in controls:
    print(repr(redact_sensitive_text(s, force=True)))
```

Observed:

| Input shape | Result |
|---|---|
| bare `m0-…` | ❌ passthrough |
| `https://api.mem0.ai/?k=m0-…` | ❌ passthrough |
| `mem0 add failed (401): key=m0-… rejected` | ❌ passthrough |
| `Authorization: Token m0-…` | ✅ masked (generic header rule) |
| `MEM0_API_KEY=m0-…` | ✅ masked (assignment rule) |
| control: `mem0_…` | ✅ masked — the pattern fires, it just matches a prefix mem0 does not issue |

So the remaining exposure is free text: error strings and log lines that carry the key inline — which is exactly the shape a 401/403 from the Mem0 API comes back in, and exactly what the terminal tool and `send_message` paths hand to `redact_sensitive_text` (`tools/terminal_tool_result.py`, `tools/send_message_senders.py`).

## Suggested fix

In `_PREFIX_PATTERNS`:

```python
r"m0-[A-Za-z0-9]{10,}",             # Mem0 Platform API key (real prefix)
r"mem0_[A-Za-z0-9]{10,}",           # legacy/alt form
```

Happy to send the one-liner alongside whatever you do for the `.` and unknown-prefix gaps.

Kanban: config knob (or tenant scoping) for the same-assignee "Recent work" injection in build_worker_context — cross-task context bleed under compaction
external_evidence.body:
## Summary

Please consider adding a configuration knob for the same-assignee "Recent work" section that `build_worker_context` injects into every Kanban worker's context — or making it opt-in. In 0.20.0 there is no way to turn it off, and on multi-tenant boards it is a cross-task context-bleed channel that compaction can amplify into a worker executing the wrong task.

## Current behavior

`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py::build_worker_context` (0.20.0) appends a `## Recent work by @<assignee>` section: the five most recent completed runs by the same profile, drawn from **unrelated tasks** (`WHERE r.profile = ? AND r.task_id != ?`). The code comment describes it as implicit role continuity ("I'm the reviewer and my last three reviews focused on security").

There is no config key, profile setting, or board setting that disables or scopes this section.

The documented `worker_context` contract (kanban tutorial, "Structured handoff — why summary and metadata matter") describes the denominator as: the task's own body, its **prior attempts**, and **parent task results**. The same-assignee section is not mentioned anywhere in the docs, so operators discover it only when it misbehaves.

## Observed failure mode (production, multi-tenant board)

We run one board with several client matters as tenants; one analyst profile serves all of them. Sequence we hit live:

1. A worker spawned on task A (matter Alpha). Its `kanban_show` output included recent-work rows for tasks from matter Beta — same profile, unrelated tenant.
2. An automatic context compaction summarized the transcript. The compaction summary preserved the foreign matter-Beta material on equal footing with task A's own identity (the summary recorded *that* `kanban_show` had been called, but not its body).
3. Post-compaction, the worker resumed "its" task using the wrong structured context: it reported a different `case_item_id`, a different matter root, and completed run metadata that belonged to the matter-Beta workflow. The run wrote no artifacts, but the task's run history now asserts the wrong matter — a human had to catch it and route a clean retry.

The injection is bounded and clearly useful for single-tenant role continuity, but on a multi-tenant board it means every worker's context carries material from other clients' tasks by default, and any context loss (compaction, session restore) can promote that material into active authority.

## Proposal

Any of these shapes would close the gap; rough order of preference:

1. **Config knob**, e.g.:

   ```yaml
   kanban:
     worker_context:
       role_history: off   # off | titles | full (default: full)
   ```

   Per-profile override would be ideal, so orchestrator lanes can keep continuity while multi-tenant specialist lanes turn it off.

2. **Tenant scoping** — when `tenant` is set on tasks, restrict the recent-work query to the same tenant (`AND t.tenant = ?`). This preserves the feature's intent while eliminating the cross-client channel.

3. **Compaction hardening** (complementary): for dispatcher-spawned workers, have the context compressor restate the runtime-pinned `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` identity in/around the compaction summary, so task ids that appear in historical evidence cannot displace the one dispatcher-pinned work authority after compaction. The docs already treat `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` as the single task authority for a worker; making compaction restate it would keep that true across context loss.

## Why not just keep a local patch?

We currently run a local patch that removes the section and adds the compaction identity restatement, reapplied after every upgrade. It works, but it is standing divergence from the released kernel — every upgrade risks silent drift, and the behavior seems generally desirable for anyone running multi-tenant boards. Happy to submit a PR for whichever shape you prefer.

[Security]: Remaining gateway authz reads can inherit another profile's environment under multiplexing
external_evidence.body:
## Bug description

This is a **gateway-level follow-up** to #93522 and #93639, not a duplicate of their adapter changes.

The adapter PRs scope authorization reads inside Weixin/Yuanbao/Signal/WeCom, but the shared authorization choke point still reads the following variables through `_auth_env()`:

- `{PLATFORM}_ALLOW_ALL_USERS` at `gateway/authz_mixin.py:577-580`
- `{PLATFORM}_ALLOWED_USERS` at `gateway/authz_mixin.py:612-613`
- `GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS` at `gateway/authz_mixin.py:619`

`_auth_env()` prefers `agent.secret_scope.get_secret()`, but on a scoped miss it falls through to the shared process environment:

```python
val = get_secret(name)
if val is not None and str(val).strip():
    return str(val).strip()
...
return (os.getenv(name) or default).strip()
```

Under `gateway.multiplex_profiles`, `os.environ` may contain the default/primary profile's first-writer-bridged authorization values. A secondary profile with an installed but empty scope can therefore inherit another profile's allow-all or allowlist value.

The same module already contains the correct scope-authoritative helper, `_platform_gate_env()` (`gateway/authz_mixin.py:46-72`), which returns the default instead of falling through to `os.environ` when multiplexing is active and the installed profile scope does not contain the key.

## Existing repository proof

Current main already includes a strict xfail that pins the remaining defect:

`tests/gateway/test_qqbot_scope_paths.py:100-121`

```python
@pytest.mark.xfail(
    reason=(
        "gateway/authz_mixin.py still reads the platform allow-all flag via "
        "_auth_env, which falls through to os.environ on a scoped miss; the "
        "scope-authoritative gate (_platform_gate_env semantics) for the "
        "remaining authz_mixin reads lands in a separate PR. Flips green "
        "when that PR converts the allow-all read."
    ),
    strict=True,
)
def test_scope_does_not_inherit_environ_opt_in(...):
    ...
```

The test sets `QQ_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true` only in `os.environ`, installs multiplex mode with an empty secondary scope, and expects the secondary profile to remain unauthorized. It currently xfails because `_auth_env()` inherits the process value.

Reviewed at main commit `96df9525299c5b54645bdebecf2f0b9ecbcd1134`.

## Relationship to existing work

- #93522 reports raw adapter-level `os.getenv()` reads in Weixin/Yuanbao/Signal/WeCom.
- #93639 fixes those adapter reads and does **not** modify `gateway/authz_mixin.py`.
- This issue tracks the explicitly deferred shared-runner reads documented by the strict xfail above.

## Security impact

Prerequisites:

1. `gateway.multiplex_profiles` is enabled.
2. The primary profile has a platform/global allow-all or allowlist value in the shared process environment.
3. A secondary profile has no corresponding value in its installed secret scope.

An external sender authorized only by the primary profile's environment can pass the shared gateway authorization check for the secondary profile. If that secondary profile exposes terminal-capable tools, the authorization widening crosses a profile security boundary.

Single-profile deployments are not affected; their existing `os.environ` fallback must remain unchanged.

## Expected behavior

When a profile scope is installed and multiplex mode is active:

- a scoped value wins;
- an absent scoped value resolves to the default/deny state;
- the process environment is not consulted for another profile's authorization policy.

Without multiplexing, legacy `os.environ` behavior should remain unchanged.

## Suggested fix

Route the remaining shared authorization reads through scope-authoritative semantics, preferably the existing `_platform_gate_env()` pattern:

- `platform_allow_all_map` read;
- `platform_env_map` read;
- `GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS` read;
- audit adjacent authorization-policy reads for the same scoped-miss fallback class.

## Regression tests

1. Remove the strict xfail from `test_scope_does_not_inherit_environ_opt_in` and make it pass.
2. Add a mirror test for `{PLATFORM}_ALLOWED_USERS` where only the primary process environment contains the sender.
3. Add a mirror test for `GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS`.
4. Preserve the existing single-profile environment fallback test.

## Audit provenance

Found during an independent read-only security review using `zai/glm-5.3` with max reasoning, then manually verified against current main. CWE-862 / CWE-200 class.

- All three reads named in the report route through it: the per-platform allow-all flag (`platform_allow_all_var`), the per-platform/group allowlists (`platform_env_map` / `platform_group_user_env_map` / `platform_group_chat_env_map`), and `GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS`.

So the deferred shared-runner reads landed; nothing left to do here as far as I can tell. Thanks for the precise chain to #93522/#93639 — the follow-up structure is what made this checkable in two minutes.

Current-main closure receipt: this report was reviewed against `96df9525299c`, but the shared-runner authz gap had already been fixed by merged #93446 at merge commit `2912c36aa41c2e33f3f61d16de0a3897a1e6cef1`. Reviewed against current `origin/main` (dbb6acd333a) in the multiplexed-gateway backlog sweep — confirming what @liuhao1024 and @andrexibiza found above.

Fixed by 2912c36aa41 (#93446, merged 2026-08-24): `_auth_env()` now delegates to `_platform_gate_env()` (`gateway/authz_mixin.py:59-69`), so the per-platform allow-all, per-platform/group allowlists, and `GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS` all stop at the routed profile's scope under multiplex instead of falling through to `os.environ`. external_evidence.title: [Bug]: Discord multiplex gateway second auth gate can apply another     profile’s allowlist after #75970
external_evidence.description:
### Bug Description

    PR #75970 fixed the adapter-level portion of #72348 by making
    Discord and Telegram allow/deny gates profile-scoped per adapter.
    
    However, the gateway’s second authorization gate still reads
    allowlist values through gateway/authz_mixin.py::_auth_env().
    When a multiplexed profile’s secret scope does not contain a
    requested value, _auth_env() falls back to process-global
    os.environ.
    
    This can make profile B’s gateway authorization decision consume
    profile A’s process-global allowlist before profile B’s
    adapter-local YAML policy is considered.
    
    A deterministic two-profile probe against the released v0.20.0
    source produced:
    
    text
    profile-A-only user on profile B: authorized
    profile-B configured user on profile B: rejected
    
    
    This issue is intended to track that residual explicitly after
    #72348 was closed as completed by #75970.
    
    Related Issues and PRs
    
    - Original issue: #72348
    - Merged adapter-level fix: #75970
    - Broader open repair carrying policy through the second gateway
    gate and persisted transport state: #76166
    
    This is not a request to revert or discredit #75970. That PR fixed
    a substantial part of the original defect, including adapter-local
    message, slash, component, backfill, allow-all,
    username-resolution, and Telegram paths.
    
    The remaining problem is the downstream gateway authorization
    boundary.
    
    Environment
    
    - Hermes Agent v0.20.0 / release v2026.8.3
    - Verified against commit 01a1037d1e6d7b6eb96a786ef282c3aea4818194
    - Linux
    - gateway.multiplex_profiles: true
    - Multiple Discord profiles with distinct credentials and
    profile-local authorization configuration
    
    Current Code Path
    
    gateway/authz_mixin.py::_auth_env() prefers the active profile’s
    secret scope, but falls back to process-global environment state
    when the scoped lookup is absent or empty:
    
    python
    def _auth_env(name: str, default: str = "") -> str:
        """Read allowlist/auth env; prefer profile secret_scope under
    multiplex."""
        if not name:
            return default
        try:
            from agent.secret_scope import get_secret
    
            val = get_secret(name)
            if val is not None and str(val).strip():
                return str(val).strip()
        except Exception:
            pass
        return (os.getenv(name) or default).strip()
    
    
    GatewayAuthorizationMixin._is_user_authorized() then uses it for
    the platform allowlist:
    
    python
    platform_allowlist = _auth_env(
        platform_env_map.get(source.platform, "")
    )
    
    
    The adapter-local config.extra["allow_from"] fallback is
    consulted only when the environment-derived allowlists are empty.
    
    Therefore, a nonempty process-global value belonging to profile A
    can prevent profile B’s adapter-local policy from being evaluated.

### Steps to Reproduce

   
    Minimal Reproduction
    
    Run from the Hermes repository root:
    
    python
    import os
    import tempfile
    from pathlib import Path
    from types import SimpleNamespace
    
    from gateway.authz_mixin import GatewayAuthorizationMixin
    from gateway.config import Platform
    from gateway.run import _profile_runtime_scope
    from gateway.session import SessionSource
    
    
    class Probe(GatewayAuthorizationMixin):
        def init(self, adapter):
            self._adapter = adapter
            self.config = SimpleNamespace(multiplex_profiles=True)
            self.adapters = {Platform.DISCORD: adapter}
            self._profile_adapters = {
                "profile-b": {Platform.DISCORD: adapter}
            }
            self.pairing_stores = {}
            self.pairing_store = None
    
        def _pairing_store_for(self, source):
            return None
    
        def _adapter_for_source(self, source):
            return self._adapter
    
        def _authorization_adapter(self, platform, profile=None):
            return self._adapter
    
        def _adapter_enforces_own_access_policy(
            self, platform, profile=None
        ):
            return False
    
    
    adapter = SimpleNamespace(
        config=SimpleNamespace(
            extra={"allow_from": "222"}
        )
    )
    probe = Probe(adapter)
    
    saved = {
        key: os.environ.get(key)
        for key in (
            "DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS",
            "DISCORD_ALLOW_ALL_USERS",
            "GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS",
            "GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS",
        )
    }
    
    Simulate profile A's value remaining in process-global state.
    os.environ["DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS"] = "111"
    
    for key in (
        "DISCORD_ALLOW_ALL_USERS",
        "GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS",
        "GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS",
    ):
        os.environ.pop(key, None)
    
    try:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
            profile_home = Path(td) / "profiles" / "profile-b"
            profile_home.mkdir(parents=True)
    
            # Profile B intentionally has no env-based Discord
    allowlist.
            # Its own policy is in adapter config.extra above.
            (profile_home / ".env").write_text(
                "# no DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS here\n"
            )
    
            with _profile_runtime_scope(profile_home):
    
                def authorized(user_id):
                    source = SessionSource(
                        platform=Platform.DISCORD,
                        chat_id="test-dm",
                        chat_type="dm",
                        user_id=user_id,
                        profile="profile-b",
                    )
                    return probe._is_user_authorized(source)
    
                print(
                    "A_USER_111_ON_B=",
                    authorized("111"),
                )
                print(
                    "B_USER_222_ON_B=",
                    authorized("222"),
                )
    finally:
        for key, value in saved.items():
            if value is None:
                os.environ.pop(key, None)
            else:
                os.environ[key] = value
    

### Expected Behavior


    text
    A_USER_111_ON_B= False
    B_USER_222_ON_B= True
    
    
    Expected Behavior
    
    When multiplexing is active and a profile scope is installed:
    
    1. A missing value in profile B’s secret scope must not fall
    through to another profile’s process-global authorization value.
    2. The selected profile’s live adapter policy must remain
    authoritative for the gateway’s second authorization gate.
    3. Profile A’s allowed users, allow-all flags, roles, channels, or
    pairing state must never authorize traffic for profile B.
    4. Profile B’s own YAML/config-based allowlist must continue to
    authorize profile B’s intended users.
    5. The same ownership must survive asynchronous boundaries such as
    restored sessions, component callbacks, background delivery, and
    voice callbacks.

### Actual Behavior

    
    text
    A_USER_111_ON_B= True
    B_USER_222_ON_B= False


    Actual Behavior
    
    A scoped miss in profile B falls back to os.environ, where
    profile A’s bridged value may be present.
    
    Because that value is nonempty, the later adapter-local
    config.extra["allow_from"] fallback is skipped.
    
    The result is both:
    
    - cross-profile false authorization; and
    - rejection of the receiving profile’s correctly configured user.
    
    Security and Isolation Impact
    
    This violates the multiplexing invariant that only the selected
    profile’s authorization policy may govern dispatch into that
    profile’s agent and tool context.
    
    The first Discord adapter admission layer is substantially improved
    by #75970, but the gateway performs an additional authorization
    decision. Restored-session, delayed interaction, voice, or other
    paths that depend on the downstream gate must preserve the
    receiving adapter/profile policy rather than re-reading
    process-global authorization state.
    
    Relationship to #76166
    
    Open PR #76166 appears to address this residual more
    comprehensively by carrying an adapter-local DiscordAccessPolicy
    and transport-owning profile through:
    
    - adapter admission;
    - the gateway’s second authorization gate;
    - pairing-store resolution;
    - persisted and restored session sources;
    - interactive component callbacks;
    - voice callbacks; and
    - transport/profile provenance.
    
    The PR is broad and may need to be rebased or split, but it should
    be linked here because it covers paths not fully closed by #75970.
    
    teknium1 also confirmed in the #76166 discussion that current
    main still contained relevant process-global Discord authorization
    inputs and noted that #76166 carries policy through the second
    gateway gate and persisted source metadata.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Discord

### Debug Report

```shell
Report       https://paste.rs/IxXis
  agent.log    https://paste.rs/bMplH
  gateway.log  https://paste.rs/K3DFd
```

### Operating System

Ubuntu

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

_No response_

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

_No response_

### Proposed Fix (optional)


    Suggested Fix Shape
    
    Possible approaches include:
    
    1. Make a profile-scoped miss authoritative under multiplexing
    rather than falling through to process-global authorization state.
    2. Route the gateway’s second authorization decision through the
    selected live adapter’s captured policy.
    3. Preserve the transport-owning profile separately from any later
    runtime-routed profile.
    4. Keep pairing stores profile-owned and fail closed when an
    explicitly stamped profile has no matching store.
    5. Ensure restored sessions and delayed callbacks recover the
    original transport policy without persisting temporary role grants
    as permanent authorization.
    
    The exact implementation can follow the maintainers’ preferred
    consolidation of #75970 and #76166.
    
    Required Regression Coverage
    
    Please add an end-to-end two-profile test covering at least:
    
    - profile A process-global user must be denied by profile B;
    - profile B YAML/config user must be accepted by profile B;
    - both adapter initialization orders;
    - explicit empty/false profile values;
    - profile-specific allow-all flags;
    - direct messages and group/channel traffic;
    - slash commands and component callbacks;
    - profile-owned pairing stores;
    - persisted/restored source ownership;
    - delayed interaction and voice paths, where applicable;
    - confirmation that single-profile behavior remains unchanged.
    
    Additional Context
    
    The original #72348 closure was understandable for the
    adapter-level fix delivered by #75970. This issue is intentionally
    narrower: it tracks the remaining gateway second-gate and
    transport-ownership boundary so the completed adapter work and the
    residual authorization work can be evaluated separately.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

--- Issue comments ---
Submitted PR #80238 to address this.

**Root cause:** `_auth_env()` in `gateway/authz_mixin.py` falls back to `os.getenv()` when the profile's secret scope doesn't contain the requested key. Under multiplex, `os.environ` holds first-writer-bridged values from another profile's YAML→env bridge, leaking profile A's allowlist into profile B's authorization decision.

**Fix:** Applied the same multiplex isolation guard already used by `_platform_gate_env()` — when a scope is installed AND `is_multiplex_active()`, absent keys return the default instead of falling through to process env. Single-profile deployments are unaffected.


Fixed on main via #93446 (2912c36aa). The root cause was `_auth_env` in gateway/authz_mixin.py falling through to `os.environ` on a scoped miss under multiplex — so a profile with no allowlist inherited another profile's process-env allowlist/allow-all values. `_auth_env` now delegates to `_platform_gate_env`, which returns the default on a scoped miss under multiplex (single-profile keeps the legacy env read). This covers the Discord second-auth-gate path and all other platform allowlist reads. Credit to @RelaxJonh (#80238) and @OWWZO (#80360) for the fix.

external_evidence.title: [Bug]: multiplex allowlists leak through _auth_env, and bot_relay puts connection_id into python -c
external_evidence.description:
### Bug Description

Two bugs, both on current main.

1. Under `gateway.multiplex_profiles`, `_auth_env` in `gateway/authz_mixin.py` still reads `os.environ` when a profile scope does not have the key. That process env can hold another profile's allowlist or allow-all flag. Profile B can then admit users (or everyone) using profile A's settings.

   `_platform_gate_env` next to it already does the right thing (scope miss returns the default). `_auth_env` is the one `_is_user_authorized` uses for platform allowlists, `GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS`, and `GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS`.

   Open PR #92895 only switches the per-platform `{PLATFORM}_ALLOW_ALL_USERS` read. It does not fix the other `_auth_env` reads.

2. `tools/bot_relay.py` `waiter_command` puts `connection_id` into generated `python -c` source. Roster rows already charset-check `handle` and `profile`, but `connection_id` only gets `.strip()`. A quote in the id SyntaxError's the waiter. A crafted id can run extra Python in the sender gateway. The Desktop already has the install's secrets, so this is not unauth RCE, but the generated source should not run roster fields as code.

### Steps to Reproduce

Allowlist leak:

1. Enable multiplex.
2. Install an empty secret scope for profile B.
3. Set `os.environ["TELEGRAM_ALLOW_ALL_USERS"] = "true"` (or `GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS`, or `QQ_ALLOWED_USERS` listing a sender).
4. Call `_is_user_authorized` for a sender that profile B never listed.

Bot-relay:

1. Pass a roster row with `connection_id` like `x'); open(r'/tmp/pwned','w').write('pwned'); print('x`.
2. `_normalize_roster_row` currently accepts it.
3. `waiter_command` builds `python -c` source that compiles and runs that extra `open()`.

### Expected Behavior

- A multiplexed profile whose scope does not set an allowlist or allow-all flag must not inherit those values from `os.environ`.
- Single-profile mode (no multiplex) still reads `os.environ` as before.
- Roster `connection_id` is charset-checked like `handle`/`profile`.
- Values put into `python -c` are encoded with `repr()`, so a quote or extra statement stays data.

### Actual Behavior

- `_auth_env("GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS")` returns `"true"` from the process env on a scoped miss. Same for platform allowlists and allow-all flags.
- `_platform_gate_env` on the same miss returns `""`.
- The existing test `test_scope_does_not_inherit_environ_opt_in` is marked xfail for this.
- `waiter_command` puts the raw id into `'Delivery to {label} failed...'`. The payload compiles and the extra `open()` runs. A benign `foo'bar` id is a SyntaxError.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp), Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp

### Debug Report

```shell
N/A. Found by reading current main and reproduced with unit tests. No live gateway session, so hermes debug share has nothing useful here.
```

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Python Version

3.11

### Hermes Version

main 0159b51f2b

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
_auth_env TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS: 'profile-A-users'
_auth_env GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS: 'true'
_platform_gate_env TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS: ''
_platform_gate_env GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS: ''

waiter payload compiles: True
injected open() ran and wrote: pwned
benign quote compiles: False (SyntaxError)
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`_auth_env` calls `get_secret()`, treats empty/missing as a miss, then always does `os.getenv`. Under multiplex, `get_secret` already returns None on a scoped miss and tells you not to read `os.environ`. `_auth_env` ignores that and reads it anyway.

`waiter_command` builds Python source with an f-string into a single-quoted string. `reply_path` uses `!r`. The label does not.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Make `_auth_env` call `_platform_gate_env`. Apply `_HANDLE_RE` to `connection_id`. Put the waiter label in source with `{label!r}`.

PR will follow this issue immediately.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

external_evidence.title: [Security]: Remaining gateway authz reads can inherit another profile's environment under multiplexing
external_evidence.description:
## Bug description

This is a **gateway-level follow-up** to #93522 and #93639, not a duplicate of their adapter changes.

The adapter PRs scope authorization reads inside Weixin/Yuanbao/Signal/WeCom, but the shared authorization choke point still reads the following variables through `_auth_env()`:

- `{PLATFORM}_ALLOW_ALL_USERS` at `gateway/authz_mixin.py:577-580`
- `{PLATFORM}_ALLOWED_USERS` at `gateway/authz_mixin.py:612-613`
- `GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS` at `gateway/authz_mixin.py:619`

`_auth_env()` prefers `agent.secret_scope.get_secret()`, but on a scoped miss it falls through to the shared process environment:

```python
val = get_secret(name)
if val is not None and str(val).strip():
    return str(val).strip()
...
return (os.getenv(name) or default).strip()
```

Under `gateway.multiplex_profiles`, `os.environ` may contain the default/primary profile's first-writer-bridged authorization values. A secondary profile with an installed but empty scope can therefore inherit another profile's allow-all or allowlist value.

The same module already contains the correct scope-authoritative helper, `_platform_gate_env()` (`gateway/authz_mixin.py:46-72`), which returns the default instead of falling through to `os.environ` when multiplexing is active and the installed profile scope does not contain the key.

## Existing repository proof

Current main already includes a strict xfail that pins the remaining defect:

`tests/gateway/test_qqbot_scope_paths.py:100-121`

```python
@pytest.mark.xfail(
    reason=(
        "gateway/authz_mixin.py still reads the platform allow-all flag via "
        "_auth_env, which falls through to os.environ on a scoped miss; the "
        "scope-authoritative gate (_platform_gate_env semantics) for the "
        "remaining authz_mixin reads lands in a separate PR. Flips green "
        "when that PR converts the allow-all read."
    ),
    strict=True,
)
def test_scope_does_not_inherit_environ_opt_in(...):
    ...
```

The test sets `QQ_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true` only in `os.environ`, installs multiplex mode with an empty secondary scope, and expects the secondary profile to remain unauthorized. It currently xfails because `_auth_env()` inherits the process value.

Reviewed at main commit `96df9525299c5b54645bdebecf2f0b9ecbcd1134`.

## Relationship to existing work

- #93522 reports raw adapter-level `os.getenv()` reads in Weixin/Yuanbao/Signal/WeCom.
- #93639 fixes those adapter reads and does **not** modify `gateway/authz_mixin.py`.
- This issue tracks the explicitly deferred shared-runner reads documented by the strict xfail above.

## Security impact

Prerequisites:

1. `gateway.multiplex_profiles` is enabled.
2. The primary profile has a platform/global allow-all or allowlist value in the shared process environment.
3. A secondary profile has no corresponding value in its installed secret scope.

An external sender authorized only by the primary profile's environment can pass the shared gateway authorization check for the secondary profile. If that secondary profile exposes terminal-capable tools, the authorization widening crosses a profile security boundary.

Single-profile deployments are not affected; their existing `os.environ` fallback must remain unchanged.

## Expected behavior

When a profile scope is installed and multiplex mode is active:

- a scoped value wins;
- an absent scoped value resolves to the default/deny state;
- the process environment is not consulted for another profile's authorization policy.

Without multiplexing, legacy `os.environ` behavior should remain unchanged.

## Suggested fix

Route the remaining shared authorization reads through scope-authoritative semantics, preferably the existing `_platform_gate_env()` pattern:

- `platform_allow_all_map` read;
- `platform_env_map` read;
- `GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS` read;
- audit adjacent authorization-policy reads for the same scoped-miss fallback class.

## Regression tests

1. Remove the strict xfail from `test_scope_does_not_inherit_environ_opt_in` and make it pass.
2. Add a mirror test for `{PLATFORM}_ALLOWED_USERS` where only the primary process environment contains the sender.
3. Add a mirror test for `GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS`.
4. Preserve the existing single-profile environment fallback test.

## Audit provenance

Found during an independent read-only security review using `zai/glm-5.3` with max reasoning, then manually verified against current main. CWE-862 / CWE-200 class.

--- Issue comments ---

Evidence:

- `gateway/authz_mixin.py` now defines `_auth_env` as a thin alias over `_platform_gate_env` (scope-authoritative: scoped miss under multiplex returns the default, no `os.environ` fallthrough; docstring cites #72348).
- All three reads named in the report route through it: the per-platform allow-all flag (`platform_allow_all_var`), the per-platform/group allowlists (`platform_env_map` / `platform_group_user_env_map` / `platform_group_chat_env_map`), and `GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS`.
- The strict xfail you quoted (`tests/gateway/test_qqbot_scope_paths.py::...::test_scope_does_not_inherit_environ_opt_in`) no longer carries the marker, and the full file passes 12/12 on current `main` — including the `QQ_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true`-in-environ-only, empty-secondary-scope case asserting the secondary stays unauthorized, and the single-profile `os.environ` regression.

So the deferred shared-runner reads landed; nothing left to do here as far as I can tell. Thanks for the precise chain to #93522/#93639 — the follow-up structure is what made this checkable in two minutes.


Current-main closure receipt: this report was reviewed against `96df9525299c`, but the shared-runner authz gap had already been fixed by merged #93446 at merge commit `2912c36aa41c2e33f3f61d16de0a3897a1e6cef1`. The quoted QQ strict-xfail is also gone and the regression is now an ordinary passing assertion on the current tree. Closing this as already resolved rather than opening a second implementation path. Provenance remains #93446 (salvage of #93159) plus the earlier adapter-side #93639 chain.

Reviewed against current `origin/main` (dbb6acd333a) in the multiplexed-gateway backlog sweep — confirming what @liuhao1024 and @andrexibiza found above.

Fixed by 2912c36aa41 (#93446, merged 2026-08-24): `_auth_env()` now delegates to `_platform_gate_env()` (`gateway/authz_mixin.py:59-69`), so the per-platform allow-all, per-platform/group allowlists, and `GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS` all stop at the routed profile's scope under multiplex instead of falling through to `os.environ`. ## Summary

The `is_safe_url()` function in `tools/url_safety.py` (lines ~9-15) resolves the hostname to an IP address and checks against blocked ranges (private IPs, cloud metadata). However, there is a **time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) gap**: after `is_safe_url()` returns True, the actual HTTP client resolves the hostname again for the connection.

## Attack Scenario

An attacker-controlled DNS server with TTL=0 can:
1. Return a public IP (e.g., `1.2.3.4`) for the safety check → `is_safe_url()` passes
2. Return a private IP (e.g., `169.254.169.254`) for the actual HTTP connection
3. The request hits the cloud metadata endpoint, bypassing SSRF protection

## Impact

SSRF protection can be bypassed to access:
- Cloud metadata endpoints (`169.254.169.254`) for credential theft on AWS/GCP/Azure
- Internal services on private networks
- Localhost services

This is particularly impactful for cloud-deployed gateway instances.

## Note

The redirect guard in `gateway/platforms/base.py:237-251` mitigates redirect-based SSRF bypasses but does not address DNS rebinding.

## Suggested Fix

Use connection-level validation via HTTP client transport hooks that validate the resolved IP address **at connection time**, not at URL-check time. For example, with `httpx`:

```python
class SSRFSafeTransport(httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport):
    async def handle_async_request(self, request):
        # Resolve and validate IP here, at connection time
        ...
```

## Severity

Warning — exploitable but requires attacker-controlled DNS infrastructure.
Fix PR: #8053. Related to #7342 (DNS pinning for SSRF protection).

external_evidence.title: [Security][HIGH] DNS rebinding (TOCTOU) bypasses SSRF protection — cloud metadata exfiltration risk
external_evidence.description:
## Summary

The SSRF protection in `tools/url_safety.py` performs a **pre-flight DNS resolution** to block private/internal IPs. However, an attacker controlling a DNS server with TTL=0 can return a public IP for the check, then switch to a private IP (e.g., `169.254.169.254`) for the actual TCP connection — bypassing the check entirely. This is a documented **TOCTOU (time-of-check, time-of-use) race condition**.

## Severity

**HIGH** — CVSS v3: `AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N` (~6.8)

## Affected Files

- `tools/url_safety.py` (line 16 — limitation documented in module docstring)
- `tools/web_tools.py:963–973` (pre-flight check applied here)

## Evidence

The codebase correctly documents the limitation:

```
# tools/url_safety.py docstring
DNS rebinding (TOCTOU): an attacker-controlled DNS server with TTL=0
can return a public IP for the check, then a private IP for the actual
connection. Fixing this requires connection-level validation (e.g.
Python's Champion library or an egress proxy like Stripe's Smokescreen).
```

The check is applied in `web_tools.py`:

```python
# tools/web_tools.py:963–973
for url in normalized_urls:
    if not await async_is_safe_url(url):   # pre-flight DNS — TOCTOU window here
        ssrf_blocked.append(...)
    else:
        safe_urls.append(url)
```

## Attack Scenario

1. Attacker registers `evil.com` with DNS TTL=0
2. Agent fetches `https://evil.com/data` via `web_extract()`
3. SSRF pre-flight resolves `evil.com` → `1.2.3.4` (public) → allowed
4. Attacker's DNS server switches response to `169.254.169.254` before the actual HTTP connection
5. Agent fetches cloud instance metadata, leaking AWS IAM role credentials, GCP service account tokens, or Azure managed identity tokens
6. In a cloud-hosted Hermes deployment this could lead to full cloud account compromise

## Recommended Fix

This cannot be fixed at the pre-flight level alone. The only reliable mitigation is **connection-level validation**:

1. **Deploy an egress proxy** (e.g., [Stripe Smokescreen](https://github.com/stripe/smokescreen)) between Hermes and the internet. The proxy validates the final resolved IP at connection time, inside the OS TCP stack where DNS rebinding cannot operate.
2. **Alternatively**, use a library like [Champion](https://github.com/nicowillis/champion) that validates the IP after `connect()` but before data is sent.
3. **Cloud-side hardening**: Enable AWS IMDSv2 with `hop-limit=1`, GCP metadata server restrictions, and Azure IMDS with firewall rules — these prevent metadata access even if SSRF succeeds.

## Additional Context

- The existing SSRF protection is well-designed and correctly blocks the vast majority of cases; this is a known hard problem at the pre-flight level
- Redirect-level re-validation via httpx event hooks (in `vision_tools.py` and gateway adapters) is already implemented — this is the right pattern and should be extended to all HTTP clients
- Reported from full architectural review of main branch (cloned 2026-06-26)


--- Issue comments ---
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Duplicate of #8033 — the DNS-rebinding TOCTOU SSRF bypass in `tools/url_safety.py` (pre-flight resolve vs. connection re-resolve) is already tracked there, with fix PR #8053. The limitation is self-documented in the `url_safety.py` docstring; a real fix needs connection-level validation (pinned-IP socket or egress proxy). Related browser-side hardening: #35236 (post-navigation CDP peer-IP validation).

Closing as duplicate of #8033, fixed on main by 8e4b5d8774 (#70193, credit @teknium1): create_ssrf_safe_[async_]client resolves once, validates the IP and connects to that pinned IP (Host/SNI preserved), closing the DNS-rebinding TOCTOU on Hermes-owned fetch paths. Reopen with a repro on a build containing that commit.

(Batch close for wave #111234; landing verified as merge commit `8e4b5d877431` on `main`.)

external_evidence.title: Security: local browser backend skips SSRF URL validation entirely
external_evidence.body:
## Summary

SSRF URL validation via `is_safe_url()` in `tools/browser_tool.py` (lines ~1301-1305) is only applied for **cloud browser backends** (Browserbase). Local browser instances (Playwright, the default) skip SSRF checks entirely.

## Impact

When the agent runs with the default local browser backend, it can navigate to:
- Internal network addresses (e.g., `http://192.168.1.1/admin`)
- Cloud metadata endpoints (e.g., `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/`)
- Localhost services (e.g., `http://localhost:8080/admin`)

A prompt injection can instruct the agent to navigate to these endpoints and exfiltrate the page content.

## Suggested Fix

Apply `is_safe_url()` checks to **all** browser backends, not just cloud ones. The SSRF risk is arguably higher for local browsers since they have direct access to the host network.

## Severity

Warning — SSRF via prompt injection against the default browser configuration.
Fix PR: #8054. Related to #16234 (hybrid browser routing SSRF bypass in cloud deployments).

Closing this as already-mitigated for the dangerous case, intentional-design for the rest. Summary (full detail in PR #8054's close comment):

- **Cloud metadata / IMDS** (`169.254.169.254`, `metadata.google.internal`, ECS task creds, Azure IMDS, IPv6) — already an **always-blocked floor** on `main` for every backend, not overridable by `allow_private_urls`. This is the credential-exfiltration scenario in this report, and it's closed.
- **General private addresses on local backends** (`192.168.x`, `10.x`, `localhost`) — intentionally skipped. The agent already reaches those over the terminal tool (`curl http://192.168.1.1/admin`), so browser-only blocking adds no security while breaking legitimate local-network browsing.
- **Sandboxed terminal** (Docker/Modal/SSH can't reach internal nets but the host browser can) — the only genuine remaining gap, handled narrowly by #38697 (Fixes #38690) via `TERMINAL_ENV`.

Thanks @tomqiaozc for the report and the fix attempt in #8054.
